send_message.name: Send message

announce.name: Announce

request_capability.name: Request capability

use_browser.name: Use browser

use_display.description: Use a display that this environment offers and permits.

shared.name: Shared writes

here.name: Here

place.name: Place

host.name: Host

link.name: Link

together.name: Use local sign-in

model.title: Model

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: The reasoning effort asked of the model, one of those the model lists.

params.title: Agent parameters
params.description: Values for the parameters that the agent's adapter declares, by parameter.

features.title: Agent features
features.description: Which optional features of agents are switched on, by feature.

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.description: Standing instructions given to the agent with every session; each scope adds its own under those above it.

memory.title: Agent notes
memory.description: Whether an agent keeps notes between sessions: through any available method, through its own program, or not at all.

messages.title: Messages to agents
messages.description: Texts that replace what Orch itself says to agents, by message.

default_provider_id.title: Default provider
default_provider_id.description: The provider that new threads here are put on.

default_agent_id.title: Default agent profile
default_agent_id.description: The agent profile that new threads here use.

subagents_at_once.title: Sub-agents at once
subagents_at_once.description: How many sub-agents the agent program may run at once. The smallest value at this place or above applies. An unsupported control says why it does not apply.

subagent_depth.title: Sub-agent depth
subagent_depth.description: How many layers of sub-agents may start; 1 allows no nesting. The smallest value at this place or above applies. An unsupported control says why it does not apply.

harness_versions.title: Agent program versions
harness_versions.description: The build each agent program uses in new or updated units, inherited through the project and overridden by the environment. An exact agent profile pin wins; changing this does not replace a running unit.

harness_channel_hours.title: Release check interval
harness_channel_hours.description: How often to read release channels when a place requests newer builds; 0 keeps scheduled reads off.

harness_interface_timeout_secs.title: Interface check timeout
harness_interface_timeout_secs.description: How long a build may take to print its interface.

harness_case_timeout_secs.title: Conformance case timeout
harness_case_timeout_secs.description: How long each native harness case may take against the scripted model.

harness_conformance_timeout_secs.title: Conformance check timeout
harness_conformance_timeout_secs.description: How long the complete native harness check may take in its isolated unit.

harness_mirror.title: Release mirror
harness_mirror.description: A server that serves the vendors' release files where this server cannot reach them.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Which skills the agents of threads here are given, by skill: off, the latest version or a pinned version; a lower place may change or switch off an inherited one.

personal_skills.title: Personal skills
personal_skills.description: Whether the agent of a thread is also given the own skills of the person who started it.

harness_trust_mirror.title: Trust mirror checksums
harness_trust_mirror.description: Allow the release mirror to publish executable checksums of its own. These builds are labelled as mirror checksums, not vendor checksums.

cwd.title: Start directory
cwd.description: Where the agent starts inside the thread's directory, as a relative path.

side_threads.title: Side threads
side_threads.description: Whether side threads may be started from the threads here.

side_max.title: Side threads at once
side_max.description: How many side threads of one thread may be open at once.

side_idle_hours.title: Side thread idle time
side_idle_hours.description: After how many hours without a turn an open side thread is closed.

inputs_without_use.title: Writers without use
inputs_without_use.description: What happens to a message for the agent from somebody who may write here but may not use the thread's model or its environment.

switch_history.title: History on a switch
switch_history.description: What a switch or a fork carries of the conversation unless its plan says otherwise.

switch_carry_share.title: Carried context
switch_carry_share.description: How much of the new model's context window a switch may fill with the conversation it carries.

native_fork_check_bytes.title: Native fork check size
native_fork_check_bytes.description: The most a conversation may take for a fork at one of its turns to be checked against the agent program's own record, so that the program can make the fork itself. A longer conversation is carried as the newest turns that fit.

read_turn_bytes.title: Turn read size
read_turn_bytes.description: The most the messages of one turn may take, written out in full, for Orch to read that turn into a summary of the conversation or a goal check; a larger turn is named and left out, and nothing of it is read.

plan_first.title: Plan first
plan_first.description: Whether the composer's Plan switch starts on for a thread's first message. The approval mode stays as it is.

plan_answered_by.title: Who answers plans
plan_answered_by.description: Who may proceed with a plan an agent proposes, or keep it planning.

max_turns.title: Goal turns
max_turns.description: The most turns a goal may use here; 0 is no limit. A goal may set its own limit unless a place locks this one.

max_minutes.title: Goal minutes
max_minutes.description: The most minutes a goal may be active here; 0 is no limit. It is looked at between turns: a running turn is not cut short.

max_credits.title: Goal credits
max_credits.description: The most credits a goal may use here, written as a decimal number; 0 is no limit. Usage caps hold as always.

mode.title: Approval mode
mode.description: When an agent has to ask before it acts: always, when it asks by itself, or never.

allowed_modes.title: Allowed approval modes
allowed_modes.description: The approval modes that may be chosen here.

mode.title: Tool access
mode.description: What the agent program lets commands do: read files, change workspace files, or use everything the environment allows.

allowed.title: Allowed models
allowed.description: Patterns naming the models that may be used here at all; a model has to be named by every scope that sets a list.

allowed.title: Allowed providers
allowed.description: Patterns over providers' Orch addresses; every scope that sets a list must admit the provider used for work here.

presets.title: Provider presets
presets.description: Ready-made API upstreams offered when a provider is added, by name; a lower scope adds one, replaces one, or hides one.

allow_http_upstreams.title: Upstreams without TLS
allow_http_upstreams.description: Whether an API endpoint may be reached without TLS, as for a model server on a private network.

expiry_notice_days.title: Expiry notice
expiry_notice_days.description: How many days before a token that a provider runs on lapses its managers are told; 0 tells them only once it has lapsed.

subscription_harnesses.title: Subscriptions allowed
subscription_harnesses.description: The agent programs whose subscriptions may be added as providers here.

subscription_sharing.title: Subscriptions shared
subscription_sharing.description: The agent programs whose subscriptions may be used by people other than their owner.

attribution.title: Attribution
attribution.description: Whether Orch's composed input, stop, denial and forwarded text names people: auto once a second person's words are delivered, always, or never (a person/an approver, with source, time and notes kept). Authored chats and documents retain their writers.

default_delivery.title: Default delivery
default_delivery.description: What an input does when a turn is running, unless its sender says otherwise: wait for the next turn, or steer the running one.

thread_default.title: New threads
thread_default.description: Whether a new thread joins the resolved default environment or is given one of its own.

default_id.title: Default environment
default_id.description: The environment new threads join when they share one and ask for no other. The creator must manage it. Clear the choice to inherit the place above.

update.title: Updates
update.description: Whether an environment that is behind waits for somebody to update it, or is updated whenever it starts.

template_id.title: Template
template_id.description: The template that a managed environment is made from.

host_id.title: Host
host_id.description: The host that a managed environment is made on; unset, the one with the most room.

storage.title: Storage
storage.description: Named machine storages for new workspace, home and connector state data. Existing data keeps its recorded location.

data_sources.title: Workspace and home
data_sources.description: Where each data root lives: made by Orch or an existing directory allowed by this machine's environment.roots. Existing directories keep their owner and mode, have no volume size limit and are never removed by a purge.

after_up.title: Commands after start
after_up.description: Named argv commands run inside a managed environment after every start; null removes an inherited name and a failure keeps the start closed.

mounts.title: Mounts
mounts.description: The mounts attached beside the workspace, each as the mount says, off, read-only, or read-only with the environment's own changes kept apart.

resources.title: Limits
resources.description: The limits of an environment's unit in place of its template's: processor, memory, processes and disk.

needs.title: Needs
needs.description: What an environment declares it needs at least, for choosing where it runs: memory, processor and disk.

idle_stop_minutes.title: Idle stop
idle_stop_minutes.description: Stop a managed environment after this many minutes without activity; 0 never stops it.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Variables given to the environment, by name.

secret_names.title: Secrets
secret_names.description: The names of the secrets that an environment is given.

idle_warning_minutes.title: Idle warning
idle_warning_minutes.description: How many minutes before an idle stop its warning is sent; 0 sends none.

removed_keep_days.title: Removed files
removed_keep_days.description: Days to keep owned files after unit removal, bounded by the system retention window; 0 makes them eligible for immediate removal.

unused_remove_days.title: Remove when unused
unused_remove_days.description: Schedule the removal of an environment made from a template once no thread has been in it for this many days; 0 never does.

lifetime.title: Lifetime
lifetime.description: Keep this environment, remove it after idle time, or also after its creating thread is archived. Only owned files are deleted.

temporary_idle_hours.title: Temporary idle time
temporary_idle_hours.description: Hours without activity before a temporary environment and its owned files are removed. Its owner gets an hour to keep or export it.

recycle_idle_minutes.title: Recycle idle time
recycle_idle_minutes.description: The idle time, in minutes, that the Recycle dialog starts from; 0 applies no minimum idle time.

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.description: Choose a runtime the host offers. Leave unset to use the template's default.

allowed_hosts.title: Allowed hosts
allowed_hosts.description: Exact other host names a restricted unit may reach; lists intersect and an empty list allows only Orch's own transport.

enabled.title: MCP servers
enabled.description: Which MCP servers are switched on, by server; a lower scope may switch an inherited one off.

offers.title: Exec offers
offers.description: How an agent running with its provider may run tools in this environment, in the order tried.

orch_tools.title: Orch's own tools
orch_tools.description: Whether the agents that work in this environment are offered Orch's own tools.

enabled.title: Orch tools
enabled.description: Which of Orch's own tools an agent is offered.

calls_per_minute.title: Tool calls a minute
calls_per_minute.description: How many calls of Orch's tools one thread's agent may make in a minute.

agent_reach.title: Agents' reach
agent_reach.description: Which other threads the agents here may read without anybody sharing them: none, those of their topic, or those of their project.

agent_documents.title: Topic documents
agent_documents.description: Whether agents may read or also edit and create public documents beside their topic and its main threads; private documents, conversations, chats, management and Export keep their own rules.

snapshot_max_bytes.title: Largest copy
snapshot_max_bytes.description: The largest copy that may be shared with an agent in one request, in bytes.

allow_external.title: Owners share outside
allow_external.description: Whether the owners of a thing here may themselves name somebody from outside its root org on its page.

external_max_days.title: Outside entries end
external_max_days.description: The longest an entry that names somebody from outside may last after it is written or renewed.

allow_holders.title: Holders share
allow_holders.description: Whether somebody who holds a thing here without owning it or managing its page may share it, at most at their own level: name others on its page, give a role in a place, share it with agents. When off, sharing is with a thing's owners and whoever manages its page.

chat_messages_per_hour.title: Agent chat messages per hour
chat_messages_per_hour.description: Successful posts across all chats from one origin in a rolling hour; zero forbids posting.

delivery.title: Announcement delivery
delivery.description: How an announcement reaches a thread whose turn is running: it interrupts, steers, or waits for the next turn.

fallback.title: When steering is impossible
fallback.description: What is done instead when an announcement is to steer an agent that cannot be steered.

wake_idle.title: Wake idle threads
wake_idle.description: Whether an announcement starts a turn on a thread that is idle.

agent_options.title: Agents' choices
agent_options.description: What an agent may choose for one announcement in place of the values set here.

rate_per_hour.title: Announcements an hour
rate_per_hour.description: How many announcements one thread's agent may send in a rolling hour; 0 allows none.

agent_scope.title: Announcement reach
agent_scope.description: How far an agent's announcement may reach: its topic, its project or its nearest org.

max_bytes.title: Largest archive
max_bytes.description: The largest archive one export of what lies here may come to, in bytes; one that would pass it is not begun, and says so with its size.

max_items.title: Most things in an archive
max_items.description: How many conversations, chats and documents one export of what lies here may hold.

keep_hours.title: Archives are kept
keep_hours.description: For how many hours a finished archive is kept for its person to fetch before it is removed.

ignore.title: Ignored paths
ignore.description: Patterns, written as in a gitignore file, for what the index of a workspace leaves out.

index.title: Index
index.description: Whether the whole tree of a workspace is indexed for use while it is offline, or only listed while its environment is online.

record_days.title: Keep turn files
record_days.description: Days to keep complete turn and restore undo files in the environment; zero disables recording.

record_max_bytes.title: Largest recorded directory
record_max_bytes.description: The included file and link bytes eligible for whole-state recording; larger directories use per-file undo.

repository_url.title: Repository
repository_url.description: The repository prepared only when the thread's directory is missing; an existing directory keeps its own files.

branch.title: Source branch
branch.description: The branch to prepare; unset, use the repository's advertised default branch.

secret_name.title: Source secret
secret_name.description: The name of an existing HTTPS Git reading secret; its value is sealed only to the preparation command.

enabled.title: Shells
enabled.description: Whether interactive shells may be opened.

record.title: Keep the last output
record.description: Whether the last of what a shell printed is kept in its environment's history when the shell closes.

detached_minutes.title: Detached time
detached_minutes.description: For how many minutes a shell keeps running with nobody attached before it is closed.

max_per_person.title: Shells per person
max_per_person.description: How many shells one person may have open at once in one environment.

max_per_environment.title: Shells per environment
max_per_environment.description: How many shells may be open at once in one environment, everybody's together.

enabled.title: Browsers
enabled.description: Whether the environments here show their browsers, start one when asked, and offer their agents the tool for them. Off, an agent may still run a browser as it runs any program.

preset.title: Browser preset
preset.description: How a browser is started where nobody says: headless, with no window and no display, or with a window on a display that Orch opens for it.

args.title: Browser arguments
args.description: Arguments added to those a browser is started with; the ones Orch gives itself, the profile's directory and the address it is driven at, cannot be set here.

viewport.title: Browser window size
viewport.description: The size of a new browser's window, written width x height, from 320x240 to 3840x2160.

idle_minutes.title: Browser idle close
idle_minutes.description: Close a browser that Orch started once it has been idle this many minutes: nobody watched or drove it and no agent's tool named it; 0 never does.

max_per_environment.title: Browsers per environment
max_per_environment.description: How many browsers that Orch started may run at once in one environment.

enabled.title: Ports
enabled.description: Whether current door holders may use owned TCP and UDP ports through Orch.

max_open.title: Wider ports
max_open.description: The distinct port numbers with wider or pending audiences; zero leaves own use available.

link_max_secs.title: Link lifetime
link_max_secs.description: The longest link lifetime from creation, including later expiry changes.

expiry_hours.title: Pending agent requests
expiry_hours.description: The longest pending boundary decision an agent requests; an earlier requested port-link lapse also ends it.

enabled.title: Displays
enabled.description: Whether the environments here show their displays, open one when asked, and offer their agents the tool for them.

geometry.title: Display size
geometry.description: The size of a display that Orch opens, written width x height, from 320x240 to 3840x2160.

max_per_environment.title: Displays per environment
max_per_environment.description: How many displays that Orch opened may run at once in one environment.

full_percent.title: Full at
full_percent.description: The share of a host's memory, declared as needed by what runs there, at which the host counts as full.

when_full.title: When a host is full
when_full.description: Whether making or moving an environment onto a full host only warns, or is refused beforehand.

idle_stop_minutes.title: Idle stop
idle_stop_minutes.description: Stop a managed provider's runtime after this many minutes without a session or a lease; 0 never stops it.

template_id.title: Template
template_id.description: The provider template that a managed provider's runtime is made from.

host_id.title: Host
host_id.description: The host that a managed provider's runtime is made on; unset, the one with the most room.

resources.title: Limits
resources.description: Limits over the template's values: processor, memory, processes and disk. The driver reports which limits it enforces.

storage.title: Storage
storage.description: Named machine storages for new provider home and connector state data. Existing data keeps its recorded location. Provider runtimes have no workspace.

home.title: Agent home
home.description: A home made by Orch or an existing directory allowed by this machine. Leave unset to keep the profile’s choice or the agent program’s default and its existing sign-in. Existing directories keep their owner, permissions and files; deleting the runtime never deletes them.

needs.title: Needs
needs.description: The processor, memory and disk a managed provider runtime declares it needs for placement.

after_up.title: Commands after start
after_up.description: Named argv commands run in the provider runtime after each start or attachment, where its machine permits them. Only its owners can change them on the provider.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Runtime variables override the template and agent profile when its runtime next starts or attaches.

secret_names.title: Secrets
secret_names.description: Names of provider secrets supplied over the profile's variables. Values are sealed to the runtime's machine, written separately and never returned.

update.title: Updates
update.description: Whether a runtime that is behind waits for somebody to update it, or is updated whenever it starts.

renew_days.title: Renewal
renew_days.description: Renew a sign-in when fewer than this many days remain, or this many days after its last renewal when its expiry is unknown; 0 switches renewal off.

created_by_members.title: Resources members may add
created_by_members.description: The kinds of resource that any member may make in an org as their own.

recreate_grace_secs.title: Recreate grace
recreate_grace_secs.description: How many seconds running turns may finish before a recreate interrupts them; 0 interrupts them immediately.

policy.title: Capability policy
policy.description: For each capability, whether a request for it is allowed, asked about or denied, and who decides.

request_expiry_days.title: Access request expiry
request_expiry_days.description: After how many days a request for access that nobody decided lapses.

max_pending_requests.title: Pending requests
max_pending_requests.description: How many requests for access one person may have waiting.

quick_grant_durations.title: Quick access durations
quick_grant_durations.description: Durations offered for giving access in one click: a positive number of days followed by d, or always.

new_color.title: New node colour
new_color.description: Whether a new place starts with its kind's icon colour or one of the twelve picked at random.

max_per_place.title: Tags on a place
max_per_place.description: How many tags one place carries at most; 0 allows none.

restricted_drivers.title: Restricted drivers
restricted_drivers.description: The drivers whose templates only system admins may define.

batch_parallel.title: Batch size
batch_parallel.description: How many switches, moves or updates of one batch run at the same time.

active_turn.title: Running turn
active_turn.description: What a switch, a move, a recreate or an update does with a turn that is running: wait for it, or interrupt it.

wait_minutes.title: Wait
wait_minutes.description: For how many minutes it waits for running turns to end before it gives up and leaves everything as it was; 0 does not wait.

verify_timeout_secs.title: Health check time
verify_timeout_secs.description: How many seconds the checks of the new side may take before everything is rolled back.

keep_previous.title: Keep the old side
keep_previous.description: Whether the side that a switch or a move leaves behind is kept instead of scheduled for removal.

batch_threads.title: Threads per batch
batch_threads.description: How many threads one batch may plan; raise this default for a larger reviewed switch.

prefer.title: Preferred agent setup
prefer.description: Ways to run an agent, tried first in this order. Other supported options follow.

allowed.title: Allowed agent setups
allowed.description: Control where agents may run and whether sign-in access may be shared with an environment.

refresh_margin_secs.title: Credential refresh margin
refresh_margin_secs.description: A shared copy of a credential that expires is renewed when fewer than this many seconds remain.

title.title: Titles
title.description: How automatic titles are written: no title, the first input, the agent’s title, or a summary.

description.title: Descriptions
description.description: Whether the summarizer keeps a description as live progress.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Whether the summarizer sets a place's tags.

topic_rollup.title: Topic description
topic_rollup.description: Whether a topic's description is summed up from those of its threads.

summarizer.title: Summarizer
summarizer.description: Which summarizer is used, and its configuration.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: When automatic titles and descriptions are written again: after a turn, at a milestone or at intervals, and how often at most.

rates.title: Rate card
rates.description: Model prices in credits, matched by model ID.

catalogue.title: Estimates
catalogue.description: Whether use that has no rate is estimated from the rate catalogue that ships with Orch.

catalogue_scale.title: Catalogue scale
catalogue_scale.description: What one unit of the rate catalogue is worth in this place's credits.

catalogue_url.title: Catalogue address
catalogue_url.description: An https address from which the system may fetch a newer rate catalogue.

catalogue_refresh_days.title: Catalogue refresh
catalogue_refresh_days.description: Every how many days the system fetches the rate catalogue by itself; 0 only when an admin asks.

enabled.title: Chats
enabled.description: Whether people may post in the chats of the nodes here.

direct.title: Direct chats
direct.description: Whether the members of a root org may start direct and group chats with each other.

group_max_members.title: Group size
group_max_members.description: How many people one group chat may have.

group_mentions.title: Role and group mentions
group_mentions.description: Who may name role and group audiences among current readers: chat writers, or chat managers; the creator manages a group chat.

attachment_max_bytes.title: Attachment size
attachment_max_bytes.description: The largest file attached to a chat message, in bytes.

person_rate_per_hour.title: Person notifications per hour
person_rate_per_hour.description: How many people one person may explicitly notify in one root org in a rolling hour; 0 disables the limit.

person_note_chars.title: Person notification note length
person_note_chars.description: How many characters an optional notification note may have; 0 allows no note.

enabled.title: Documents
enabled.description: Whether new documents may be made beside the nodes here.

templates.title: Starting documents
templates.description: Current readable ordinary documents offered when creating one here; a template grants no source access or creation permission.

max_bytes.title: Document size
max_bytes.description: The most text one document here may hold, in bytes.

max_blocks.title: Document blocks
max_blocks.description: The most blocks one document here may have.

versions_kept.title: Versions kept
versions_kept.description: How many versions of one document here are kept at most.

history_max_bytes.title: History size
history_max_bytes.description: How much the kept versions of one document here may take together, in bytes.

file_max_bytes.title: File size
file_max_bytes.description: The largest one file a document here may hold, in bytes.

files_max_bytes.title: Files together
files_max_bytes.description: The most the files of one document here may come to together, in bytes.

description_chars.title: Document description length
description_chars.description: Characters the summarizer may write for a document's description.

shown.title: Links tabs
shown.description: The tabs of a document's Links section that its readers see. A document's owner can switch tabs off for one document; a lock here decides for the whole place.

page_size.title: Links page size
page_size.description: Rows shown in a Links list before Show more.

occurrences.title: Mentions per source
occurrences.description: Mentions listed under one source in Referenced by before Show more.

line_chars.title: Mention line length
line_chars.description: Characters of the line shown around each mention in Referenced by.

mentions_counted.title: Mentions counted
mentions_counted.description: Mentions of the document counted in one source before its count reads “or more”.

access_checks.title: Links access checks
access_checks.description: Sources whose reading access is checked for one page of Referenced by. A very popular document continues with a cursor.

graph_nodes.title: Graph nodes
graph_nodes.description: The most nodes the Links graph draws.

enabled.title: Semantic search
enabled.description: Also find results with a similar meaning, using the embeddings below.

embeddings.title: Embeddings
embeddings.description: Provider and model that compute embeddings; their use is counted to whoever names them.

max_disk_share.title: Disk limit
max_disk_share.description: Index size limit as a share of the indexed content's size; indexing pauses at the limit. Empty: no limit.

tuning.title: Indexing and ranking
tuning.description: How text is split, embedded and ranked.

reorder_window_secs.title: Reorder window
reorder_window_secs.description: How long new results may reorder the first screen.

meaning_pause_ms.title: Typing pause
meaning_pause_ms.description: How long typing pauses before an embeddings request, in milliseconds.

vector_cache_secs.title: Vector cache
vector_cache_secs.description: How long an org reuses a query vector for the same model.

word_recent_candidates.title: Recent word sample
word_recent_candidates.description: Recent rows sampled before probing the text index.

cursor_ttl_secs.title: Search lifetime
cursor_ttl_secs.description: How long a search's continuation stays available.

vector_cache_entries.title: Query cache size
vector_cache_entries.description: Query vectors cached per org; zero disables caching.

word_candidates.title: Word candidates
word_candidates.description: Candidates per indexed field before exact access and ranking.

word_probe_candidates.title: Word index probe
word_probe_candidates.description: Indexed matches sampled before switching to a recency scan.

word_tuning.title: Word retrieval
word_tuning.description: Estimated rows below which word search uses native scoped reads. Missing field limits use Word candidates. Windows per request defaults to one; Show more continues.

archive_idle_days.title: Archive idle topics
archive_idle_days.description: Archive a topic after this many days without activity; 0 never does.

delete_archived_days.title: Delete archived nodes
delete_archived_days.description: Delete a node this many days after it was archived; 0 never does.

agent_history_idle_days.title: Agent history kept
agent_history_idle_days.description: Remove a thread's agent history after this many days without a turn; 0 never does.

inbox_days.title: Inbox kept
inbox_days.description: For how many days a notification stays in a person's Inbox, read or not, before it is removed.

mask_secrets.title: Mask secrets
mask_secrets.description: Whether the values of the secrets a thread was given are masked in stored text.

patterns.title: Patterns
patterns.description: Further patterns to mask in stored text, each with a name.

retention_days.title: Diagnostics kept
retention_days.description: For how many days diagnostics are kept.

personal_closed.title: Personal orgs closed
personal_closed.description: Whether a person's own org is created taking no member but its person.

personal_flat.title: Personal orgs flat
personal_flat.description: Whether a person's own org is created holding no org inside it.

created_by.title: Who may make an org
created_by.description: Who may make a team org: anybody signed in, system admins only, or somebody a system admin invited to make one, each invitation used once. Personal organization creation is a separate policy.

personal_enabled.title: Create personal organizations
personal_enabled.description: Give new accounts a personal organization. Disabling this keeps existing organizations; people can still join teams and receive document shares.

order.title: Order of the tree
order.description: The order in which the org's tree is shown to whoever follows the org's own: as somebody arranged it, the newest first, the most recently changed first, or by name. An owner or admin of the org saves it from the order they see.

mode.title: Registration
mode.description: Who may register: nobody, only somebody with an invitation, or anybody who reaches the system.

email_verification.title: Email verification
email_verification.description: Whether a person has to confirm their address before they sign in.

forms.title: Invitation forms
forms.description: The forms of invitation that may be made for an org of this tree: a link to share, a personal link for one address, or both.

default_hours.title: Invitation life
default_hours.description: For how many hours an invitation is good when its inviter says nothing.

max_hours.title: Longest invitation
max_hours.description: The most hours an invitation may be good for.

max_uses.title: Uses of a shared link
max_uses.description: How many people one shared link may bring in at most.

shared.title: Shared mail server
shared.description: Whether a root org that has no mail server of its own sends its mail through the system's.

check_days.title: Look for a release
check_days.description: Days between read-only checks of the operator's configured release source; 0 is off. A check sends no installation statistics and installs nothing.

warn_days.title: Database backup warning
warn_days.description: Warn when the last successful database-only backup is older than this many days. A failed attempt does not make it newer.

local_login.title: Password sign-in
local_login.description: Whether people other than system admins may sign in with a password or a mailed code.

email_code.title: Code by mail
email_code.description: What a code sent to a person's confirmed address may be when they sign in: a way in by itself, a second step after the password, both or neither.

second_step.title: Second step
second_step.description: Whether the people of this org need a second proof set up and given before they work here.

max_days.title: Longest token life
max_days.description: The longest total life of an API token that is admitted here: from when it was made to when it ends.

banner.title: Banner
banner.description: A message shown to everybody on the system, with its level and when it ends.

allowed_private_hosts.title: Private hosts
allowed_private_hosts.description: The private hosts that org or personal channels and destinations, and skill archive addresses, may reach.

max_blob_bytes.title: Largest file
max_blob_bytes.description: The largest single file that Orch stores, in bytes.

env_cache_quota_bytes.title: File cache
env_cache_quota_bytes.description: How many bytes of cached file contents are kept for one environment.

max_bytes.title: Skill size
max_bytes.description: The most bytes the files of one version of a skill hold together.

max_files.title: Skill files
max_files.description: The most files one version of a skill holds.

rules.title: Call recovery
rules.description: Ordered rules for retrying, continuing, failing over or waiting after a model call fails.

repeat_limit.title: Repeat limit
repeat_limit.description: Automatic recoveries of one failure kind within the repeat window; zero stops automatic recovery.

repeat_window.title: Repeat window
repeat_window.description: The rolling time window used to stop repeated recovery.

notify_on_stop.title: Notify on stop
notify_on_stop.description: Tell the thread owner once when the repeat guard stops recovery.

return.title: After failover
return.description: Return to the thread’s own choice at the next turn when ready, or stay on the candidate.

measurement_keepalive_secs.title: Keep counts running
measurement_keepalive_secs.description: Seconds a count keeps running after its last plan closes.

measurement_valid_secs.title: Reuse counts
measurement_valid_secs.description: Seconds a completed count stays valid for another plan.

measurement_timeout_secs.title: Counting time
measurement_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a machine may take to finish a count.

stall_secs.title: Unchanged progress
stall_secs.description: Seconds without changed progress before the job names the wait.

stop_wait_secs.title: Stopping wait
stop_wait_secs.description: Seconds before an unconfirmed stop names its machine.

io_timeout_secs.title: Copy time
io_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a machine may take to finish one file operation.

preview_bytes.title: File preview size
preview_bytes.description: Bytes a reference card reads for a text excerpt.

preview_lines.title: File preview context
preview_lines.description: Lines shown before and after a referenced line; 0 shows only the referenced line.

paste_inline_context_share.title: Pasted text in the message
paste_inline_context_share.description: The default share of remaining context for pasted text. 0 always sends it as a file; 100 always sends it in the message. The sender can choose for each paste.

unused_keep_days.title: Clean unused caches
unused_keep_days.description: Days to keep images and tool versions that nothing uses; 0 switches automatic cleanup off. Data follows its own retention dates.

release_keep_count.title: Keep unused releases
release_keep_count.description: Unused releases kept per payload after an update; 0 keeps all. Current and previous releases are always kept.

subagents.title: Sub-agent notices
subagents.description: Whether the people who follow a thread are told when one of its sub-agents finishes, fails or is stopped, as they are told when a turn ends.

operations.title: Operation notices
operations.description: Whether Notify starts ticked in an operation: when work is blocked, always, or never. The person confirms the choice; recipients keep their own notification choices.

preview_source_bytes.title: Preview source size
preview_source_bytes.description: The largest original decoded for a static file preview.

preview_pixels.title: Preview image pixels
preview_pixels.description: The largest image decoded for a static preview, checked before allocating pixels.

preview_edge.title: Preview dimensions
preview_edge.description: The longest edge of a static file thumbnail, in pixels.

preview_bytes.title: Preview size
preview_bytes.description: The most encoded bytes in one static thumbnail or text excerpt.

preview_cache_bytes.title: Preview cache
preview_cache_bytes.description: Bytes kept for derived previews; older previews are discarded first, and zero disables caching.

viewer_bytes.title: Media viewer size
viewer_bytes.description: The largest original image, PDF, audio or video file read into a browser viewer.

native_image_bytes.title: Native image size
native_image_bytes.description: The largest image sent natively to a model; larger images are delivered by path, and zero always uses paths.

weights.title: Related weights
weights.description: Weights from zero to one for meaning, place and references, as decimal text. Zero leaves a signal out.

place_scores.title: Related places
place_scores.description: Scores from zero to one for the same folder, topic, project or org.

count.title: Related items
count.description: Items shown in Related. Zero switches it off.

candidates.title: Related candidates
candidates.description: Candidates per signal and reference neighborhood before exact reading-access checks.

max_bytes.title: Import size limit
max_bytes.description: The expanded bytes allowed in one import. When unset, the place's export size limit applies.

max_items.title: Import item limit
max_items.description: The objects allowed in one import. When unset, the place's export item limit applies.

runtimes.title: Runtimes
runtimes.description: Allow, forbid or require runtimes by name. Use * for every runtime not named.

handoff_input_share.title: Summary input share
handoff_input_share.description: How much of the summary model's context window a hand-off, a fork or a goal check may fill with the conversation it sends: the newest turns first, older ones as their one-line index.

helpScreenReview.empty: No qualifying thread or environment is available. You can continue with the example.
helpScreenReview.exampleNote: This is an example. It changes nothing in your work.

parameters.title: Approval mode
parameters.detail: On request lets the agent program ask when a decision is needed. Changing a mode does not answer Orch's capability, port or access requests.
parameters.label: Mode

approval.title: A request before an action
approval.detail: Read the action and who may decide. Allow once permits only this request; Deny keeps it from running.
approval.label: Action

ports.title: A program's port
ports.detail: Here uses your own door. A wider opening names a place, a host audience or holders of a link.
ports.label: Port

grants.title: Allow a kind of port opening
grants.detail: Allow once applies to this request. Grant to this environment also permits later requests of the same kind.
grants.label: Audience

template.title: What new environments start with
template.detail: A template can give new environments a port capability at creation. Existing environments keep their current grants.
template.label: Starting capability
template.value: Open ports for a place's viewers

policy.title: A decision made ahead of time
policy.detail: A place can allow this capability, ask its approver or deny it. Read the place named beside the current rule.
policy.label: Decision

environment-settings.title: Review a memory change
environment-settings.detail: A driver that supports live limits applies this while work continues. Otherwise the page offers the required update before it changes the unit.
environment-settings.label: Memory

network.title: Read the program's outbound reach
network.detail: Restricted permits the configured destinations. Open also lets a program create its own outbound tunnel; a port door does not prevent that.
network.label: Network

capability.title: See when a capability takes effect
capability.detail: Supported KVM and Docker access become available without stopping work. A replacement first says its time, size and what files it keeps.
capability.label: Effect

permissions.title: Read access before sharing
permissions.detail: Owners hold the whole thing. General access chooses an audience; Custom shows the individual permission rows.
permissions.label: General access

holders.title: A role belongs to a place
holders.detail: Choose the real person, group or role from the picker. Its human label includes its place, so equal names do not become the same audience.
holders.label: Example holder

resources.title: Resource controls
resources.about: These are the controls this runtime provides. Enforced ceilings are shared by the processes it starts.

disk.name: Disk

player.title: Tutorial
player.missing: Open the screen or panel described in this step. The frame appears when its control is visible; if you cannot reach it, leave and return later.
player.picture: A topic holds the team's conversation and the agent's work. People write to each other in chat; the agent receives only an input sent to its thread.

news.title: What is new
news.about: These notes ship with the application. Open a guide to see how its controls work.
news.approvals: One request contract: two authorities, four approval modes, and a current scoped approver on each card.
news.ports: Port audiences are capabilities: grant once to an environment, use template defaults, or allow through a place's policy.
news.live: Supported limits, placed mounts, KVM and Docker access can change live. A same-image recreate keeps the unit's own files and tells you its cost first.
news.holders: The same holder picker names people, groups and roles at their places; the chain of why and explicit admin overrides stay visible.

approvals.about: Understand a mode and a request using your own work or an illustration.
approvals.one: Choose one of your threads below to read its Parameters, or continue with the example. On request means the agent program asks when it needs a decision; no mode change is needed for this lesson.
approvals.two: Open Approvals to read an existing request's action, audience and approvers. If none is waiting, the example shows the same choices without starting work.
approvals.three: Read the decision before choosing it. An agent action request follows its approval mode; capabilities, ports and access keep their own boundary approval. Continuing this lesson sends no answer.

ports.about: Read the port audiences and the ways to allow them, without opening a door.
ports.one: Choose one of your environments below to open Ports. It is fine if no program is listening yet: the example shows a port and its private Here address.
ports.two: Read the capability grants for that environment. A place, host audience and link audience are different choices. The example compares Allow once with a grant for later requests; you do not need to grant either.
ports.three: The Templates screen shows what new environments start with. A template can give a port capability at creation; the illustrated card shows that default if you have no template to inspect.
ports.four: Read the place named beside a capability's current rule. It may allow, ask or deny before a request arrives. The example uses ordinary choices, and changing a port audience does not restrict a program's outbound network.

live.about: See what changes while work continues and what needs a reviewed replacement.
live.one: Choose one of your environments below to read Settings. The example changes memory from 2 GiB to 4 GiB: a live change keeps work running; another driver first offers the required update.
live.two: Read the same environment's Network section. It says where a program may connect out. The illustrated restricted network is separate from who may enter through an Orch port.
live.three: If a capability request is waiting, read its stated effect in Approvals. Otherwise use the example: supported KVM or Docker access can become available now, while a replacement first states what it keeps, its size and its estimated time.

access.about: Read who has access and why, using your own place or a labelled example.
access.one: Choose one of your threads below to open Access. Read its owners and General access first. The example begins private; you do not need to add anyone or change a permission.
access.two: The holder picker lists the people, groups and roles visible to you, with their real places. Choose from that list rather than copying a sample address; the example shows how a role's place distinguishes it.
access.three: Read a permission row's source and chain of access. A nested group or inherited role explains why someone holds it. An admin override is explicit and recorded; it is separate from the agent's Bypass mode.

firstThread.about: Start agent work beside the team's conversation.
firstThread.one: Open a topic and choose New thread. Keep the topic's chat for messages to people; the new thread is where you ask the agent to work.
firstThread.two: In the agent composer, use a concrete input such as 'Explain the login failure before changing files.' Read the selected provider and environment, then send only when you intend to start that work.
firstThread.three: Watch the conversation in that thread. Open a turn to read its work; teammates can talk in the topic's chat without sending another input to the agent.

stepIn.about: Add direction to work already in progress.
stepIn.one: Open a running thread and read the latest turn. What the agent is doing belongs to this thread, while the topic's chat stays between people.
stepIn.two: At the composer, write the direction you mean to send and inspect its delivery choice. A draft alone changes no running work; Send, Wait and Interrupt have the effects shown by the control.
stepIn.three: Find Stop. Stop ends the current work and holds queued inputs; resume only the inputs you want. The tutorial presses neither Stop nor Send for you.

share.about: Give a colleague access to the thread and the things it uses.
share.one: Open the thread's Share page. Read Can view, Can edit and Can manage before adding anybody.
share.two: Pick a colleague by visible name and place and select the access you mean. For example Can edit lets them talk to this agent; it gives them no use of a provider by itself.
share.three: Review what goes with the thread: its model/provider and environment doors. Let them in or ask their current managers as the page offers, then confirm only the reviewed changes.

permission.about: Understand one permission page before changing it.
permission.one: Open Access on a thing you can see. The short form shows owners and the three choices; By area shows the individual doors.
permission.two: Read a holder with its place and inherited source. Developers of Web and Developers of another project are different holders.
permission.three: Read who may name holders and what is locked above this place. Use View as to inspect a person's result; an admin override is a separate explicit, audited act.

computer.about: Connect your own computer while keeping its local limits visible.
computer.one: Open Machines and choose Add machine. Environment, Agent and Provider combine in orch-connector. Node uses its own program, orch-node; using both on one computer takes two enrollments, as a host and as a machine.
computer.two: Choose the roles, which roles hand their settings to Orch, and whether to enable Full control. The displayed command follows those choices. Run it yourself only if you intend to connect the computer, and share no token.
computer.three: When the computer appears, read its Policy tab. Roles handed to Orch can be edited on Overview; otherwise use the machine’s displayed command and restart its connector. An online row means it connected; a timeout or refusal keeps its reason.

provider.about: Add a provider and make its actual models available.
provider.one: Open Providers and choose Add provider. Pick the vendor and authentication form you actually have; a label alone is no sign-in.
provider.two: In the form, name it, for example Team API, and follow its sign-in steps. The tutorial stores no key and fills no credential for you.
provider.three: Return to Providers and open its Models tab after it is ready. Choose only the models you may use and share the provider deliberately; a setup or expiry failure is shown as such.

code.about: Read and edit the same files as the agent.
code.one: Open a thread's Files view and open a source file in Code. Its path is relative to the bound environment; use your own private draft when changes should stay separate.
code.two: Read the Code status bar: saved, draft, read-only or conflict. Edit and Save only a change you intend; someone else's newer text is compared instead of overwritten.
code.three: Return to the conversation and open a turn's file difference. Review what the agent changed before publishing it, and keep unrelated staging intact.

write.about: Write beside a teammate without losing either draft.
write.one: Open a document you may edit and have a teammate open that same document. The page's authors and presence tell you whose words you see.
write.two: Write in separate blocks, then try the same block together. A conflicting newer block stays, and the other draft is offered beside it rather than silently replacing it.
write.three: Read the page's save state and history. Offline edits wait for reconnect; resolve a conflict explicitly and leave each person's authored text intact.

knowledge.about: Let an agent read what the team has shared.
knowledge.one: Open Access on the document or chat the agent should read, then its Agents tab. Choose Read or Edit for work at the intended place; a human holder and an agent share are different.
knowledge.two: Open the receiving thread's Knowledge view. It lists only what that agent may reach now, with its source; a missing item asks you to inspect the share, not guess a document id.
knowledge.three: Ask the agent to read the named material in its composer. A tool read is visible in the turn; taking the share back removes its next access and starts no turn.

usage.about: Read actual usage and the limit that applies to your input.
usage.one: Open your Usage and limits page. Tokens are reported use; an approximate price says where its rate came from, and unknown use stays unknown.
usage.two: Read the allowances below it: the period, your present count and whether the cap applies to you or shared work. A limit of 100 credits per month is different from a provider's own vendor limit.
usage.three: Open a thread's Usage view or a held input's limit explanation. Read the actual source and next reset; raising a cap, using an authorized exception and switching provider are distinct actions.

helpRelease.subagentExample: Set agents.subagents_at_once to 4 and agents.subagent_depth to 1 on an org: every thread below it may run four sub-agents at once, and those sub-agents start none of their own. A smaller child value narrows the bound; a larger one cannot relax it. The shipped values are 8 and 1. The harness enforces the limits; an unsupported control says why it does not apply.
helpRelease.mcpRestartExample: Example: Browser tools fails with exit 1 after three crashes. Read its last output with secrets masked, then choose Restart on that server. Its failure count clears and it starts again; the environment, other servers and running turns continue. Tools refresh now where the harness supports reload, otherwise before its next turn. Environment Manage is required; the job shows success or the new failure reason.
helpRelease.environmentRestartExample: Example: a turn is running and capability.recreate_grace_secs is 120. Restart… shows the turns, shells, browsers, displays and port connections that will stop. Wait lets turns finish during that grace, then interrupts any still running; Interrupt now does so immediately. The same unit stops and starts, keeping every file, including /opt/restart-proof.txt outside the volumes. Queued inputs continue when it is ready; each thread names who restarted it. The job reports an actual failure if it cannot return.

help.name: How this installation works
help.description: A connector runs as your account and works in the folders you register, independently of the terminal’s current folder. Its per-user service is systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS or a logon task on Windows. Linux user services stop at logout unless an operator enables lingering. A named instance has its own data, identity and service. A node runs as root, one per machine; share its host through Access to serve other places. The complete foreground command installs and starts it in this terminal; Ctrl+C stops it. Uninstall previews the files and asks for the enrolled name. Without --purge, data and identity stay. With --purge, it also removes owned data.
