policy.harnessesHint: One for each line: the kind of the harness, then the path of its program.

storages.title: Storage
storages.meaning: Named directories where this machine may make persistent data. One available storage may be the default.

drivers.title: Drivers
drivers.meaning: Choose the drivers this node offers and their image, registry, capability, runtime, host-account and launch-program limits. Templates stay within them. Privileged containers require an explicit allowance. Driver connections and newly enabled drivers take effect after restarting the node; permission reductions apply immediately.

resources_max.title: Resource limits
resources_max.meaning: The largest CPU, memory, process and disk declarations accepted for units on this machine. Its facts say which limits it enforces.

environment_roots.title: Directories for environments
environment_roots.meaning: Directories inside which an environment of this machine may have its root, and a mount its location.

hooks.title: Lifecycle programs
hooks.meaning: Programs run before and after start or attach, and stop or detach. Use absolute paths for pre_up, post_up, pre_down and post_down; timeout_secs bounds each run.

ports.title: Port audiences and public listener
ports.meaning: Choose allowed audiences (place, link, host). A public host listener also needs publish with incoming_address, listen and ranges. Templates may narrow these choices.

environment_remote_write.title: Writes from outside
environment_remote_write.meaning: Whether file writes arriving through Orch are accepted: what people upload and edit there.

environment_terminal.title: Shells
environment_terminal.meaning: Whether interactive shells may be opened on this machine through Orch.

environment_after_up.title: Commands after start
environment_after_up.meaning: Allow named commands after an environment or provider starts or attaches. A failed command keeps it unavailable.

environment_browser.title: Browsers
environment_browser.meaning: Allow browsers to be started, shown and driven through Orch.

environment_vnc.title: Displays
environment_vnc.meaning: Allow virtual displays and announced VNC servers, including a served local desktop.

mcp_import.title: Importing MCP servers
mcp_import.meaning: Whether the MCP servers that the harnesses here have configured may be listed for Orch and imported.

mcp_add.title: Adding MCP servers from Orch
mcp_add.meaning: Whether an MCP server may be written from Orch for an environment of this machine. Such a server is a command that runs as the connector's user.

exec_offers.title: What the exec node may offer
exec_offers.meaning: The tools this machine may run for agents working elsewhere.

environment_deliver_files.title: Files that arrive with a message
environment_deliver_files.meaning: Whether attachments, forwarded files and shared copies are written into the workspace's .orch directory.

agent_max_sandbox.title: Maximum tool access
agent_max_sandbox.meaning: The broadest tool access the server may request for an agent program here.

provider_signin.title: Sign in to a provider from Orch
provider_signin.meaning: Allow sign-in, sign-out and renewal in the person's own harness home. Homes Orch owns use the same sign-in methods without changing the person's login.

provider_upstreams.title: Where model calls may go
provider_upstreams.meaning: Base addresses this machine may forward model calls to.

provider_arrangements.title: Ways a key kept here may be used
provider_arrangements.meaning: Where agents may run and how they may use sign-ins or keys kept on this machine.

machine_roles.title: Change offered roles
machine_roles.meaning: When handed to Orch and enabled, machine managers may change this connector’s Environment, Agent and Provider roles. A local value always holds; Node uses orch-node.

agent_programs.title: Agent adapter registration
agent_programs.meaning: When handed to Orch and enabled, machine managers may register and remove agent adapter programs. An explicit local off value always holds.

provider_programs.title: Provider source registration
provider_programs.meaning: When handed to Orch and enabled, machine managers may register and remove provider source programs. An explicit local off value always holds.

agent_harnesses.title: Agent programs that may run
agent_harnesses.meaning: The agent programs this machine may run, each with its program path.

tools_fetch.title: Downloading builds
tools_fetch.meaning: Whether this machine may download and run the agent and tool programs Orch selects.

policy_delegated.title: Handed over to Orch
policy_delegated.meaning: The limits that may be changed from Orch instead of on the machine.

driverFaults.type: The value has the wrong type
driverFaults.extra: The object contains a member this configuration does not accept
driverFaults.choice: The value is not an allowed choice
driverFaults.range: The number is outside the allowed range
driverFaults.length: The text has a length outside the allowed range
driverFaults.format: The text does not have the required format
driverFaults.list: The list does not meet the required length or uniqueness
driverFaults.rule: The value does not meet this configuration rule
driverFaults.schema: The driver reported an invalid configuration schema

edit.reportedWhy: The machine reports it itself, and it changes when the machine does.
edit.connectorWhy: The connector is updated on the machine, not from here.

lost.lead: It cannot connect any more. Enroll it again to give it a new certificate: it keeps its name, its page and everything registered from it.

again.title: Enroll {{name}} again
again.lead: Run this command on {{name}}. It gets a new certificate and is the same machine afterwards.
again.goesOld: Its old certificate: it is revoked when the new one is first used, so that an old disk is out
again.goesRevoked: Nothing more: its old certificate was revoked already

certificate.title: Its certificate
certificate.lead: The certificate is what makes the machine this machine to Orch.
certificate.renewsByItself: The connector renews it by itself

list.lead: The subscriptions and keys that agents reach their models through: what you run work on, and what you look after.
list.label: Providers
list.name: Name

noneLead.mine: Add a provider on an API key, or register a login a harness already holds from the page of its machine.

overview.needsRuntimeLead: Open the runtime to finish starting this provider and see any failed step.
overview.checkSetupLead: The provider has not reported why setup is incomplete. Review its configuration and refresh its details.
overview.needsKeyLead: It has no key yet, and cannot be used before it has one and a model that may be chosen.
overview.needsModelLead: Choose at least one model and switch it on before this provider can be used.
overview.needsSignInLead: Its sign-in is missing or about to end.

key.title: Key
key.heldByOrch: Orch holds the key. It is written once and never shown again.
key.onMachine: The key is kept on {{machine}}. Replacements are sealed for that machine and never shown again.
key.secretsLead: Headers whose values are secrets. Replace one by writing a new value.
key.endpointsLead: The addresses this key opens, each with the format it speaks there.
key.changed: Somebody changed this provider first. It was read again, so what you see now is theirs; make your change again.

runtime.title: Its runtime
runtime.lookedAfter: This runtime follows its machine's declared services and policy. Configure its variables, secrets and commands here.
runtime.keeperPlace: Credential keeper: {{machine}}. This is independent of where its runtime runs.
runtime.keeperWaiting: The credential keeper will be assigned when its runtime starts.
runtime.harnessesLead: One for each agent profile in use, with its sessions.
runtime.noHarnesses: No harness has been started for this provider yet. One is started by the first turn.
runtime.restarted: The harness of {{name}} was restarted; its sessions reopen at their next turn
runtime.limits: Limits of the machine that concern it
runtime.limitsLead: What the machine allows for providers, read-only.

models.title: Models
models.noneLead: Add one below, or take the models the endpoint suggests.
models.addLead: Enter the model ID supplied by the provider.
models.routingHint: Sent to the endpoint exactly as you type it. It cannot be changed once the model is added.
models.routingEmpty: Give the name that is sent to the endpoint.
models.displayHint: Use a recognizable name for the model picker. Names must be unique within this provider.
models.rateLead: Credits per million tokens. Without a rate the use is counted in tokens and is counted by no cap in credits.
models.rateTierHint: The rate is multiplied by this for turns at that speed: 2 for double.
models.suggestionsNote: Only models listed here can be used. Suggestions are detected best-effort.
models.noSuggestions: The endpoint suggests no model that is not listed.

arrangements.title: How agents may run on this provider
arrangements.lead: The types its owner allows. Each says what it puts into an environment.

separated.name: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.separated.name)
separated.what: The agent runs here, and only its tool calls reach the environment. Nothing leaves.
separated.leaves: Nothing leaves the provider in this type.

key_separated.name: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.key_separated.name)
key_separated.what: The agent runs in the environment with its own tools and calls the model through Orch, which adds the key. The environment holds only a pass that works through Orch.
key_separated.leaves: Only a pass that works through Orch leaves; the key stays here.

credential_shared.name: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.credential_shared.name)
credential_shared.what: The agent runs in the environment on a copy that this provider issues and renews.
credential_shared.leaves: A copy of the credential may leave this provider and be held by an environment. Whoever can use that environment can read it there.

handed_over.name: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.handed_over.name)
handed_over.what: The whole sign-in goes to one environment at a time, and nobody else can use this provider until it comes back.
handed_over.leaves: The whole sign-in leaves this provider and goes to one environment at a time. Nobody else can use the provider until it comes back.

together.name: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.together.name)
together.what: The harness and its tools run together in the environment.
together.leaves: Nothing of this provider is handed over for it. Whether a thread may be placed this way is decided by the binding settings, not by this provider.

arrangements.unavailable: No agent that can run on this provider can be placed this way.
arrangements.defaultShared: Agents that keep their tools inside themselves will run in the environment on a shared token.
arrangements.defaultHere: Agents that keep their tools inside themselves will stay with the provider and work with Orch's tools.
arrangements.machineRestricted: The machine keeping this credential limits which ways can be enabled.

threads.title: Threads bound to it
threads.lead: The threads that run on this provider and that you may view, of whatever org.
threads.hiddenName: A thread you may not see
threads.none: No thread is bound to it
threads.hidden_one: and {{count}} more that you may not see
threads.hidden_other: and {{count}} more that you may not see

danger.deleteBody: The provider and its saved model list and settings are deleted.
danger.deleteKey: Its key and the secret headers of its endpoints are deleted.
danger.deleteToken: Native sign-out is requested. A token you pasted stays valid at its vendor until you revoke it there.

add.title: Add provider
add.nativeKeeperFixed: This native profile is registered on {{machine}}; its sign-in stays there. Choose the runtime independently.
add.name: Name
add.arrangements: How agents may run on it

edit.kindSubscriptionWhy: A subscription's harness holds its sign-in, and neither changes after the provider is added.
edit.kindApiWhy: Whether a provider is a subscription or an API key is chosen when it is added.
edit.runsWhy: Where its runtime is made is chosen when the provider is added.
edit.runsMachineWhy: It runs on {{machine}}, from which it was registered.

bulk.disableBody: No thread can start a turn on them until they are enabled again. Turns that are running go on to their end.

configTrust.found: {{harness}} found a configuration of its own in this environment's workspace:
configTrust.trustMeans: Trust: {{harness}} uses it as it does in a folder it trusts: its settings, servers, hooks and command rules apply to every session here.
configTrust.keepOutMeans: Keep it out: {{harness}} works here without it, as in a folder it does not trust, and then reads this workspace's instruction files (such as AGENTS.md) no more either.
configTrust.remembered: The answer is kept for this environment and can be changed on its page.
configTrust.waiting: Waiting for whoever manages {{environment}} to say whether {{harness}} may use the configuration its workspace holds.
configTrust.title: Harness configurations in the workspace
configTrust.lead: What a harness found of its own in this workspace, and whether it may use it. A directory a harness made for itself and left empty is not asked about.
configTrust.none: No harness has found a configuration of its own here.

list.lead: The places agents work in: directories on your machines and environments made from templates on hosts.
list.label: Environments
list.noMachineWhy: Add a machine first; an environment on a machine is a directory there.
list.name: Name
list.noneLead: An environment is where a thread works. Register a directory on one of your machines, and threads can run in it.
list.makeFromTemplateWhy: Orch makes it on a host.

act.keep: It counts as in use now, so the idle timer starts over

overview.imageFailed: Make the template's image available on this host, then retry. Pulling or loading it failed ({{reason}}). Check the image name and registry access, or build and publish it.
overview.hostCapacityFailed: The host lacks capacity ({{reason}}). Free the affected resources and retry.
overview.removalScheduled: It is scheduled to be removed on {{time}}

removeReason.request: Someone asked for it to be removed.
removeReason.switch: Its place was switched, so this one is no longer needed.
removeReason.unused: Nothing has used it for a long while.

threads.title: Threads in it
threads.lead: The threads that run in this environment, and the directory each works in.
threads.hidden_one: {{count}} more thread runs here in a place you cannot see.
threads.hidden_other: {{count}} more threads run here in places you cannot see.

limits.title: What this machine allows
limits.lead: The limits that {{machine}} keeps for environments on it. Each says who set it and whether you may change it.

danger.disableLead: Stops turns and units; keeps volumes
danger.enableLead: It is disabled. Enabling it lets work be put in it again.

remove.threads_one: {{count}} thread is bound to it and loses its place.
remove.threads_other: {{count}} threads are bound to it and lose their place.
remove.inUse: It is refused while something still depends on it. Move those threads first.

make.title: Add environment
make.name: Name
make.noHost: No host takes new environments with this template's driver now. Enroll one, or open a closed host.
make.mostRoom: The one with the most room
make.hostUnavailable: Choose a host that can make environments from this template.
make.noTemplate: No template to make it from
make.noTemplateLead: A template for environments that is switched on is needed. Write one under Templates.
make.hostNoDriver: its driver does not make environments

edit.runsWhy: Where it runs is chosen when it is made: a directory stays on its machine, and one made from a template stays on its host until it is moved.
edit.settingsValue: Its own values and their sources

bulk.disableBody: No thread can start a turn in them until they are enabled again. The threads bound to them keep their place.

list.lead: Agent profiles you may use or manage, with the program and settings each one uses.
list.label: Agent profiles
list.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, program, owner or machine
list.name: Name
list.noneLead: Add a profile here, or register an installed agent program from its machine’s page.

overview.notReported: This agent program has not reported yet
overview.notReportedLead: Its features appear when a machine or running provider with this program connects.
overview.bindingsLead: Where this agent program can work and who runs its tools.
overview.capabilitiesLead: Features this agent program reports. Other features are not offered on its threads.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.noneLead: Parameters appear after the agent program reports them.

profile.title: Profile
profile.lead: The name, the version to run, and the rest of the profile as JSON. A change is kept only if nobody else changed the profile since you opened it.
profile.name: Name
profile.pinHint: Default follows the environment or runtime policy; an exact pin wins
profile.jsonHint: An object. The version above is written into it as harness_version.
profile.jsonInvalid: This is not a JSON object.

danger.disableBody: Running turns stop now; waiting messages keep their order

edit.harnessWhy: The agent program is chosen when a profile is made and stays with that profile.
edit.usableWhy: A profile that was not made from a machine can run on any runtime.
edit.usableMachineWhy: It was made from {{machine}}, so it can run there only.
edit.onHint: Switching off stops its running turns immediately and keeps the profile.

machineStorage.title: Storage
machineStorage.lead: Named places where this machine makes owned data. Choose these names in environment or runtime unit configuration.
machineStorage.none: This machine has not reported an available storage.

ptrace.name: Ptrace
ptrace.description: Let debuggers inspect processes, subject to the machine's policy.

kvm.name: KVM
kvm.description: Use hardware virtualization when the host offers /dev/kvm.

gpu.name: GPU
gpu.description: Use graphics devices offered by the host.

net_admin.name: Net admin
net_admin.description: Allow network administration within the container.

unconfined.name: Unconfined
unconfined.description: Relax container security profiles for tools that need it.

privileged.name: Privileged
privileged.description: Request broad host privileges; the host must approve them.

host_network.name: Host network
host_network.description: Use the host's network instead of the container's separate network.

docker_socket.name: Docker socket
docker_socket.description: Let tools use the host's Docker service.

docker_inside.name: Docker inside
docker_inside.description: Let tools run Docker of their own inside the environment.

bridge.name: Bridge
bridge.description: Connect through a separate network under the outgoing-connection policy.

none.name: None
none.description: Reach Orch alone through the host's proxy.

restricted.name: Restricted
restricted.description: Reach Orch and host names in the place's allow-list.

open.name: Open
open.description: Use the runtime's full file permissions.

volume.name: Volume
volume.description: Keep data in a volume that outlives the container.

bind.name: Bind
bind.description: Expose a directory from the host.

provider.name: Provider data
provider.description: Read provider details, list models or supply sign-in access.

translator.name: API format support
translator.description: Convert model requests between API formats.

adapter.name: Agent program
adapter.description: Connect an agent application to Orch.

executor.name: Environment tools
executor.description: Run tools here for an agent working elsewhere.

never.name: Never
never.description: Leave the program stopped after it exits.

on-failure.name: On failure
on-failure.description: Restart only after a failed exit.

always.name: Always
always.description: Restart after both successful and failed exits.

all.name: All
all.description: Show environment and provider templates.

environment.name: Environment
environment.description: Give threads a workspace, home and tools.

provider.name: Provider
provider.description: Keep a provider's credential and run its harness.

image.name: Image
image.description: Pull an existing image from a registry.

build.name: Dockerfile
build.description: Build an image on a host that offers builds.

archive.name: Archive
archive.description: Load an image from an uploaded Docker or OCI archive.

archive.name: Archive
archive.description: Use files from an uploaded build-context archive.

git.name: Git
git.description: Use a public repository at a chosen revision and directory.

docker.name: Docker
docker.description: Make containers from images on a host that runs Docker.

host.name: Host
host.description: Run processes under an existing machine account.

json.name: JSON
json.description: Edit the same configuration as JSON; fix invalid JSON before switching back.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Allow new units to be made from this template. Existing units keep running when switched off.

none.name: No host available
none.description: No host is enrolled or shared with you yet. Enroll one or ask its owner for access.

offline.name: Enrolled but offline
offline.description: These hosts are enrolled. Reconnect a matching host before starting work from this template.

unreported.name: No matching driver reported
unreported.description: Hosts are enrolled, but no matching driver is available from their reports for this template. Ask a host operator to check its drivers.

hostAdvice.offlineUnknown: {{name}} · offline; the disconnection time was not recorded
hostAdvice.cached: You can write and save using the driver's last reported form. Starting work also needs an available host with that driver.
hostAdvice.noSchema: A host must report its driver's form before examples can be loaded or a template can be checked.

editor.invalidJson: Enter valid JSON with an object at its root.
editor.schemaMissing: No host has reported this driver's configuration schema. Ask a host operator to connect one.
editor.unset: not set; use the image, host or place settings
editor.valid: Configuration checked. Nothing has been saved.

node.name: Node
node.description: A Node web project with four cores and 4 GiB of memory; install project dependencies in its workspace.

python-db.name: Python
python-db.description: Python connecting to a separately managed PostgreSQL service. Replace the database address and select credentials through secret names.

rust.name: Rust
rust.description: Rust with Cargo and the compiler in the image, ready for Rust sources.

kvm.name: KVM
kvm.description: Choose a host labelled kvm. Environments also request the KVM capability; host approval and /dev/kvm are required. A label alone grants no device to a provider runtime.

restricted.name: Restricted
restricted.description: Reach Orch and names in the place's network.allowed_hosts allow-list. Set that list before starting and choose a host that supports restricted egress.

host-account.name: Host
host-account.description: Run printf after start as the existing agent account. Choose an account and installed programs available on your hosts before saving.

image.title: Image reference
image.description: The image to pull from a registry. Use a tag to start, or pin a digest for repeatable starts. Choose an image, a build or an archive.

image_digest.title: Pinned image digest
image_digest.description: Keep the image fixed even if its tag changes. Leave unset to follow the image reference.

build.title: Build from a Dockerfile
build.description: Build an image on a host that offers builds when the project needs additional tools.

dockerfile.title: Dockerfile
dockerfile.description: The complete Dockerfile text. The host uses the classic Docker builder before starting the unit.

context.title: Build context
context.description: Files available to COPY and ADD, from an uploaded archive or a public Git repository. Leave unset if no other files are needed.

blob.title: Context archive hash
blob.description: The 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters identifying a previously uploaded build context archive.

git.title: Public Git repository
git.description: The repository address for the context, accessible without credentials. Choose a revision and directory too.

ref.title: Git revision
ref.description: A branch, tag or commit. A commit makes the context repeatable.

path.title: Context directory
path.description: The directory within the repository. A dot uses its root.

args.title: Build arguments
args.description: Plain variables passed to Dockerfile ARG. They are stored visibly; keep secrets out.

target.title: Build stage
target.description: A named Dockerfile stage. Leave unset to build its last stage.

archive.title: Load an image archive
archive.description: Load a previously uploaded Docker or OCI image archive instead of pulling or building an image.

blob.title: Image archive hash
blob.description: The 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters identifying the uploaded image archive.

image.title: Image in the archive
image.description: The image name when an archive contains several. Leave unset when there is only one.

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.description: Leave unset for the host's default runtime. Choose runc, runsc or kata only when the host offers it.

user.title: User
user.description: Who runs the connector and commands inside the unit. Unset uses the image's user; numeric IDs take precedence over a name.

name.title: User name
name.description: An account already present in the image. Change it only when that image supplies the account.

uid.title: User ID
uid.description: Numeric user ID inside the unit. Match writable image files; zero runs as root.

gid.title: Group ID
gid.description: Numeric group ID inside the unit. If omitted with a user ID, it uses the same number.

resources.title: Limits
resources.description: The most a unit may use. Unset amounts come from resolved place settings; the host reports which limits it enforces.

cpu_millis.title: Processor time
cpu_millis.description: Thousandths of a core: 1000 is one core and 4000 is four. Raise this for parallel builds.

memory_mb.title: Memory
memory_mb.description: Memory limit in MiB; 1024 MiB is one GiB. Raise it for large builds or language servers.

memory_swap_mb.title: Memory and swap
memory_swap_mb.description: Combined memory and swap in MiB. Set memory too; this must be at least the memory limit.

pids.title: Processes and threads
pids.description: The combined process and thread limit. Raise it when builds reach the process limit.

disk_gb.title: Disk
disk_gb.description: Disk limit in GB. Enforcement requires host storage quotas; otherwise usage is reported.

blkio_weight.title: Disk priority
blkio_weight.description: Relative disk access weight, 10–1000. Higher values get more disk time under contention; host support is required.

resources_max.title: May be raised to
resources_max.description: The largest limits an environment manager may request. Initial limits must fit within these ceilings.

needs.title: Needs free
needs.description: Capacity a host must have free for placement. This declares a need without reserving resources or setting limits.

cpu_millis.title: Processor time
cpu_millis.description: Free processor capacity needed for placement, in thousandths of a core. This is not a usage limit.

memory_mb.title: Memory
memory_mb.description: Free memory needed for placement, in MiB. This does not reserve it.

memory_swap_mb.title: Memory and swap
memory_swap_mb.description: Declared combined memory and swap need, in MiB. This sets no usage limit.

pids.title: Processes and threads
pids.description: Declared process and thread capacity needed for placement.

disk_gb.title: Disk
disk_gb.description: Free disk needed for placement, in GB. This does not reserve it.

blkio_weight.title: Disk priority
blkio_weight.description: Declared relative disk weight, 10–1000. It does not reserve disk bandwidth.

network.title: Network
network.description: How the unit reaches Orch and other services. Restriction requires a host with verified proxy isolation.

mode.title: Network connection
mode.description: Bridge permits network access under the egress policy. None reaches Orch alone through the host's proxy.

egress.title: Outgoing connections
egress.description: Restricted reaches Orch and names in the place's network.allowed_hosts setting. Set its allow-list before starting.

dns.title: DNS servers
dns.description: Name server IP addresses. Empty uses network defaults; restricted and Orch-only networks require an empty list and use the proxy resolver.

security.title: Confinement
security.description: Container security options. Add privileges only when tools need them and host policy permits them.

read_only_rootfs.name: Read only
read_only_rootfs.title: Read-only image files
read_only_rootfs.description: Prevent writes to image files. Workspace, home and writable mounts remain writable; add temporary storage if tools need it.

no_new_privileges.name: No new privileges
no_new_privileges.title: Prevent extra privileges
no_new_privileges.description: Prevent processes gaining privileges after launch. Enable when tools do not rely on setuid programs.

cap_add.title: Added kernel capabilities
cap_add.description: Linux capabilities to add. Leave empty unless a trusted tool requires one; host policy still applies.

cap_drop.title: Removed kernel capabilities
cap_drop.description: Linux capabilities to remove. ALL drops every optional capability; check that the image works with it.

env.title: Variables
env.description: Plain variables stored visibly in the template. Select credentials through secret names; Orch's launch variables cannot be replaced.

mounts.title: Extra storage
mounts.description: Volumes, memory storage or host directories in addition to managed state. Targets must not overlap each other or Orch's directories.

type.title: Storage kind
type.description: Volume keeps data, tmpfs holds temporary data in memory, and bind uses a host directory. Bind needs a source; tmpfs has none.

source.title: Storage source
source.description: A Docker volume name or absolute host directory. Leave unset for a new volume or for tmpfs.

target.title: Path inside the unit
target.description: An absolute destination outside workspace, home and Orch's directories.

read_only.title: Read-only storage
read_only.description: Allow reads while preventing writes through this attachment.

host_labels.title: Required host labels
host_labels.description: The host must carry every listed label. Select suitable machines by their devices or tools.

workspace_mount.title: Workspace path
workspace_mount.description: Absolute path of the environment's persistent workspace. Match project commands; provider runtimes have no workspace.

home_mount.title: Home path
home_mount.description: Absolute path of the persistent home. Match the image user's home to keep tools and caches across starts.

base_capabilities.title: Capabilities enabled initially
base_capabilities.description: Capabilities requested on creation, subject to host policy and approval. KVM needs its host device.

allowed_capabilities.title: Capabilities that may be requested
allowed_capabilities.description: Capabilities a manager may request later. Host policy and approval still apply.

sandbox.title: Tool confinement
sandbox.description: Agent file access inside the container, separate from its isolation from the host.

default.title: Initial tool access
default.description: Read only prevents writes, workspace permits workspace writes, and open uses the container boundary. The adapter must support it.

max.title: Widest tool access
max.description: The widest file access permitted. It must allow the initial mode.

agent_defaults.title: Agent defaults
agent_defaults.description: Agent settings such as approval.mode supplied by this environment. Place settings can override them.

exec.title: Tools for agents
exec.description: Tools offered to an agent running elsewhere, in preference order.

offers.title: Available tools
offers.description: Tools in the order tried. Choose those installed in the image or supplied by the host.

orch_tools.name: Orch tools
orch_tools.title: Offer Orch tools
orch_tools.description: Allow Orch's shared tools when the adapter supports them. Disable to omit them from the session.

colocated_harnesses.title: Agents available here
colocated_harnesses.description: Installed agent applications allowed to run here. The provider's owner must also allow this setup.

mcp_server_ids.title: Tool server presets
mcp_server_ids.description: IDs of existing MCP server presets to enable on creation. Choose presets you may use.

after_up.title: Commands after start
after_up.description: Repeatable named commands run as the unit user before readiness on each new start, in name order. A failure fails the start; arguments are literal.

name.title: Command name
name.description: A unique name. Use a number prefix when execution order matters.

command.title: Program and arguments
command.description: An executable in the image followed by literal arguments. A shell runs only when explicitly named.

timeout_secs.title: Time limit
timeout_secs.description: Maximum running time, 1–3600 seconds. A timeout fails the start and stops the command group.

init.title: Earlier startup command
init.description: An earlier format, treated as the command init. Prefer Commands after start.

plugins.title: Registered programs
plugins.description: Programs installed in this image to read provider details, connect agents or supply tools. They run where the provider's sign-in is kept.

kind.title: Program kind
kind.description: The connector interface this program declares it implements.

name.title: Registered name
name.description: A unique name which cannot replace a built-in implementation. Select the program by this name.

command.title: Program and arguments
command.description: The program path inside the image followed by literal arguments. It must implement the plugin transport.

env.title: Program variables
env.description: Additional plain variables; unit variables are inherited. Keep secrets out of this visible map.

restart.title: Restart policy
restart.description: On failure restarts failed programs, always also restarts clean exits, and never leaves exited programs stopped.

list.lead: The configurations that environments, and the runtimes of managed providers, are made from.
list.label: Templates
list.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, driver, owner or image
list.name: Name
list.noneLead: A template says what an environment is made of. Once a host reports a driver, you can write one here.

overview.offLead: Nothing new is made from it. What was made from it keeps running.
overview.confinementLead: What the configuration states about holding in what runs in it. The driver's own defaults apply to the rest.
overview.confinementNone: The configuration states none; the driver's defaults apply.
overview.usesLead: The most a unit may use, how far that may be raised for one environment, and what a host must have free before a unit is placed on it.
overview.execLead: How a harness that runs elsewhere reaches this unit, in the order the offers are tried.

spec.title: Template configuration
spec.name: Name
spec.invalid: This is not a JSON object.

danger.disableLead: Nothing new is made from it until it is enabled again. What was made from it keeps running.
danger.disableBody_one: {{count}} unit was made from it and keeps running.
danger.disableBody_other: {{count}} units were made from it and keep running.
danger.enableLead: It is disabled. Enabling it lets units be made from it again.
danger.deleteUsed_one: {{count}} unit was made from it and still stands, so it cannot be deleted. Disable it instead.
danger.deleteUsed_other: {{count}} units were made from it and still stand, so it cannot be deleted. Disable it instead.
danger.deleteBody: The template is removed for good.
danger.inUse: It is refused while units made from it still stand. Remove those first.

edit.kindWhy: Whether a template is for environments or for providers' runtimes is chosen when it is made, and does not change afterwards.
edit.driverWhy: The driver is chosen when a template is made.

bulk.disableBody: Nothing new can be made from them until they are enabled again. What was made from them keeps running.

kubernetes.description: Run environments in a Kubernetes cluster.

image.description: Pull an image from a registry; pin a digest for repeatable starts.

security.description: The workload cannot gain extra privileges; it can use only capabilities approved for this cluster.

requests.title: Kubernetes requests
requests.description: Resources the Kubernetes scheduler reserves when placing a Pod.

cpu_millis.title: CPU request
cpu_millis.description: Kubernetes reserves this many thousandths of a CPU when it schedules the Pod.

memory_mb.title: Memory request
memory_mb.description: Kubernetes reserves this much memory in MiB when it schedules the Pod.

driverFeatures.title: Features
driverFeatures.about: The operations this driver offers. Unavailable features show their reason; a dash means no feature facts were reported.

list.lead: The machines that run environments and the runtimes of managed providers: whose each is, what it has and how full it is.
list.label: Hosts
list.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, label, owner, machine or driver
list.name: Name
list.noneLead: A host is a machine that runs environments for Orch. Enroll one with the command this button gives you.

add.title: Add host
add.homeHint: The org the host will belong to.

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.lead: Full is counted from what the environments here declare they need, not from what they use now. A declaration reserves nothing, so it can pass the whole.
capacity.over: More is declared than the host has.

storages.title: Storages
storages.lead: The named places on the host where volumes can be kept, as it reports them.
storages.name: Name

drivers.title: Drivers
drivers.lead: What this host can make units with.
drivers.name: Driver

settings.takeLead: Pausing a host stops new environments from being placed on it. What already runs there goes on.
settings.fullLead: Full is counted from what environments declare they need. This is what the host does when a new environment would not fit, or declares too little room. A choice is saved as soon as you make it.
settings.fullFollows: This host follows the system's answer: {{value}}.
settings.name: Name
settings.changedLead: It was read again; it is now at revision {{revision}}. Look at what changed, then save again.

runtimes.title: What runs on it
runtimes.lead: Stop an environment or provider running here, or delete it after confirming its name.
runtimes.noneLead: Units appear here when an environment is made on this host.
runtimes.successor: Being prepared to take over from another unit
runtimes.interruptTitle: Stop {{name}} and interrupt what runs in it?
runtimes.interruptBody: Turns that are running in it are interrupted, not finished.
runtimes.removeBody: It stops running on {{host}} and is deleted.
runtimes.removeProviderBody: The unit on {{host}} is deleted; the provider stays and its next turn makes a new unit.
runtimes.inUse: It is refused while something still depends on it.

provider-kind.title: What you have
provider-kind.what: A provider is how agents reach a model: through a subscription you sign in to, or through an API key.
provider-kind.which: Choose a subscription when your agent program signs in to one. Choose a key for a vendor API or your own model server.

endpoint-format.title: Format
endpoint-format.what: How the endpoint speaks: the shape of its requests and answers. An agent can use an endpoint only in a format it speaks.
endpoint-format.which: The one the vendor documents for the address you gave. A gateway that serves one key in two formats takes two endpoints.

home.title: Belongs to
home.what: The org this belongs to. Its admins look after it, and its page follows that org's defaults.
home.which: Your own org if it is only yours. A team's org if the team is to look after it.

who-may-use.title: Who may use it
who-may-use.what: What the people you choose may do with it: use it, not change it. Its owners can change who that is later, on its page.
who-may-use.which: Only me while you try it. Everyone in the org to share it with all of them. As the org decides to follow the org's own rules.

key-place.title: Where the key is kept
key-place.what: Held by Orch: Orch stores the key and sends it with each request. Kept on one of your machines: it never leaves that machine.
key-place.which: Held by Orch is simplest. Keep it on a machine when a key must not be stored elsewhere.

arrangement-separated.title: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.separated.name)
arrangement-separated.what: The agent runs at the provider and only its tool calls reach the environment. Nothing of the sign-in leaves.
arrangement-separated.which: The safest. Take it when the agent's tools can be reached from here, or the environment is not fully trusted.

arrangement-key_separated.title: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.key_separated.name)
arrangement-key_separated.what: The agent runs in the environment with its own tools and calls the model through Orch, which adds the key. The environment holds only a pass that works through Orch.
arrangement-key_separated.which: When the agent needs its own tools in the environment but the key must not enter it.

arrangement-credential_shared.title: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.credential_shared.name)
arrangement-credential_shared.what: The agent runs in the environment on a copy of the credential that this provider issues and renews.
arrangement-credential_shared.which: When the agent must work on its own inside the environment and you trust that environment with a token.

arrangement-handed_over.title: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.handed_over.name)
arrangement-handed_over.what: The whole sign-in goes to one environment at a time, and nobody else can use this provider until it comes back.
arrangement-handed_over.which: Rarely: only for a harness that cannot work on a copy.

arrangement-together.title: $t(choiceCatalog.arrangement.together.name)
arrangement-together.what: The harness and its tools run together in the environment.
arrangement-together.which: Whether a thread may be placed this way is decided by the binding settings, not by this provider.

model-efforts.title: Efforts
model-efforts.what: How hard the model is asked to think, where it takes an effort setting. A thread starts with the one marked.
model-efforts.which: Offer fewer where the model gains little from more.

model-speeds.title: Speeds
model-speeds.what: Service tiers beside the ordinary one, such as a faster mode. Each is off until a manager switches it on.
model-speeds.which: Switch one on only if people should be able to choose it: a faster speed is counted at its own rate.

model-programs.title: Access programs
model-programs.what: Programs the plan offers for this model. Each is off until a manager switches it on.

model-context.title: Context
model-context.what: How much of the conversation the model holds at once. Its own window is what the harness works with when told nothing; the largest is what the model can be given.

model-rate.title: Rate
model-rate.what: What a million tokens of this model cost, in credits. It makes use count in credits as well as in tokens.
model-rate.which: Leave it empty to use the rate card, or an estimate where Orch knows the model's family.

machine-provider-source.title: What it uses
machine-provider-source.what: The sign-in the provider works with: either the login a harness already holds on that machine, or an API key that you type on the machine itself.
machine-provider-source.which: The login if the harness there is signed in. A key when you have one and want it kept on that machine.

env-root.title: Directory
env-root.what: The folder on the machine that becomes the environment's workspace. The machine checks it against the places it allows.

env-remote-write.title: Allow writing from outside
env-remote-write.what: Lets people change files here from the web, not only the agents that run in it.
env-remote-write.which: Switch it off for a directory that should only be read.

env-terminal.title: Allow a terminal
env-terminal.what: Lets people open a shell in it. A shell runs with the rights of the user the environment runs as.
env-terminal.which: Keep it off unless people really need a shell there.

env-template.title: Template
env-template.what: The recipe the environment is made from: its image, limits and tools.
env-template.which: The default, unless you need something it lacks.

env-host.title: Host
env-host.what: The machine the environment is made on. Left open, the host with the most room is chosen.

env-runtime.title: Runtime
env-runtime.what: What holds the environment in: a container that shares the host's kernel, a kernel written in user space, or a virtual machine with a kernel of its own.
env-runtime.which: The default, unless the work needs Docker inside or a stronger boundary: then choose a runtime with a kernel of its own.

host-schedulable.title: Takes new environments
host-schedulable.what: While it is on, new environments can be placed on this host. Off, nothing new is placed and what runs stays until it is moved.

host-when-full.title: When it is full
host-when-full.what: What the host does when environments declare more than it has: warn and place anyway, or take nothing more. Full is counted from what environments declare they need; nothing is reserved.
host-when-full.which: Warn for a host that can grow on demand. Take nothing more where room is fixed.

host-labels.title: Labels
host-labels.what: Words you give a host to tell hosts apart, such as docker or arm64. They are shown and searched; they place nothing by themselves.

host-volumes.title: Its volumes
host-volumes.what: A unit's volumes keep its files and its sign-in. Removing the unit leaves them unless you tick this.
host-volumes.which: Leave it unticked if the unit may be made again with its data.

machine-delegate.title: Let its limits be changed from Orch
machine-delegate.what: Off, the machine's limits can only be changed on the machine itself. On, whoever manages what is registered from it can change the keys you hand over.
machine-delegate.which: Leave it off for a personal computer.

agent-pin.title: Version it runs
agent-pin.what: Which build of the harness this profile runs. The default build is the one the system recommends.
agent-pin.which: Pin one only to keep an agent on a version you have tested.

agent-profile.title: Profile
agent-profile.what: What the harness is started with, as JSON: its own settings, its environment variables and its version pin.

agent-harness.title: Agent program
agent-harness.what: The program that runs the agent. A profile is made for one program and keeps it.

finder-modes.title: The signs of the finder
finder-modes.what: One field finds names, settings, commands, help and what was said. A sign at the start keeps it to one kind of answer.
finder-modes.which: > to do something, @ to find a person, : for a setting, ? for help, / to search what was said. With no sign it looks everywhere.

search-results.title: Search results
search-results.what: Words and similar meaning arrive in one list; Show more continues it.

semantic-search-index.title: Semantic search
semantic-search-index.what: Choose embeddings, watch indexing and decide how to change models.

search-scope.title: Where to search
search-scope.what: The search looks through everything you may read. Naming a place keeps it to that place and what lies in it.
search-scope.which: Use Place to keep word and meaning results to a place, chat or document.

search-file-type.title: File type
search-file-type.what: Some conversation files have no recorded type. Choose Any to include them.

search-kinds.title: What to look in
search-kinds.what: Conversations with agents are made of messages, answers, reasoning, commands and more; chats and documents are looked in as well.

search-when.title: Dates
search-when.what: Keeps the search to what was written between two days, counted in your own time zone.

find-in-conversation.title: Find in the conversation
find-in-conversation.what: Looks for words in this thread alone and brings each hit into view, lit where it stands.
find-in-conversation.which: Enter goes to the next older hit, Shift+Enter to a newer one.

export-what.title: What goes in
export-what.what: A place that is ticked takes everything in it. Untick a folder, a topic, a thread or a document to leave it out.
export-what.which: To export the whole place, leave everything ticked. To export some of it, untick the rest.

export-format.title: Format
export-format.what: Markdown is written to be read, in any text editor. JSON holds the same things as records, for a program to read.
export-format.which: To read it, or to give it to an agent: Markdown. To process it with a script: JSON.

export-place-format.title: Format
export-place-format.what: Markdown is for reading; JSON is for programs. A place can also be exported as an importable Orch package.
export-place-format.which: Choose a package to import the place again.

import-review.title: Review
import-review.what: Review actions, people, conflicts and what will not be imported. The review creates nothing.

import-run.title: Import
import-run.what: The import continues if you close this dialog. Choose whether to receive a notice.

export-detail.title: How much of a conversation
export-detail.what: What was said gives each turn in a few lines. With each step adds a line for every step the agent took, and everything adds what each step was given and what came back.
export-detail.which: For a summary: what was said. To follow the work: with each step. To check exactly what ran: everything.

export-left-out.title: Left out
export-left-out.what: A thing you may read and may not take away as a file is not in the archive, and is counted here. Whoever manages it can give you the right.

export-kept.title: How long it is kept
export-kept.what: The archive stays for you to download again until this time is up or you remove it. Then it is removed from the server.

export-span.title: Span of days
export-span.what: Only the turns and the messages of these days (UTC) go in. Documents are written as they stand.

line-thread-view.title: Can view
line-thread-view.what: Watch it and take part in its chat.

line-thread-interact.title: Can interact
line-thread-interact.what: Also drive its agent: send to it, steer it, stop it, put in order what waits.

line-thread-manage.title: Can manage
line-thread-manage.what: Also set it up: its model and effort, its agent’s parameters, its instructions and its provider; answer what the agent asks, rename it and delete it. Where it runs, and who reaches its files and a terminal, is decided on its environment’s page.

line-topic-view.title: Can view
line-topic-view.what: See the topic, its threads and its chat.

line-topic-interact.title: Can contribute
line-topic-interact.what: Also start threads in it and set its status and tags.

line-topic-manage.title: Can manage
line-topic-manage.what: Also rename it, change its description and its settings, choose its default environment, and delete it.

line-project-view.title: Can view
line-project-view.what: See the project, its topics and its chat.

line-project-manage.title: Can manage
line-project-manage.what: Also rename it, change its description and its settings, move it and delete it.

line-org-view.title: Can view
line-org-view.what: See the org, its members, the orgs inside it and its projects.

line-org-manage.title: Can manage
line-org-manage.what: Also rename it, change its settings, make orgs inside it, move it and delete it.

line-document-view.title: Can view
line-document-view.what: Read it, its earlier versions and who wrote them.

line-document-interact.title: Can edit
line-document-interact.what: Also change its title and its blocks.

line-document-manage.title: Can manage
line-document-manage.what: Also put an earlier version back, move it, delete it and manage comments.

line-environment-view.title: Can view
line-environment-view.what: See the environment, look at its files and its processes, and watch its browsers and displays.

line-environment-manage.title: Can manage
line-environment-manage.what: Have all of it: put threads into it and decide where each one runs, start, stop and update it, change its settings and secrets, change its files, open a shell, drive its browsers and work in its displays; move it and remove it.

line-resource-view.title: Can view
line-resource-view.what: See it in lists, with its status.

line-resource-interact.title: Can use
line-resource-interact.what: Use it for work, within what the entry allows.

line-resource-manage.title: Can manage
line-resource-manage.what: Change it, enable and disable it, and delete it.

share-choice.title: What they can do
share-choice.what: Three choices name several permissions at once, so that nobody has to say them row by row. The full form under By area shows every row.
share-choice.which: To let someone follow along: Can view. To let them work with it: Can interact. To let them also set it up: Can manage.

share-reach.title: What sharing a place gives
share-reach.what: Sharing a place with everything in it gives a role there, so the person holds in everything inside what its pages give that role. Sharing the place itself names them on its own page only: they see it, its chat and its documents, and nothing inside.
share-reach.which: To share a folder with what lies in it: choose everything in it. To let someone see the place and nothing else: choose only the place.

share-export.title: Take it away as a file
share-export.what: As it is shipped, whoever may read a thing may also export it as a file. Untick this to let them read it here and not take it away.

share-tell.title: Tell them
share-tell.what: Each person named gets one message from you in the chat the two of you have, with the link and a line you may write. Without it they are told nothing: the thing is simply there for them.

share-outside.title: Share outside
share-outside.what: A person from outside the org gets access to this one thing and nothing else of the org. Who may name them is a row of the page, which as shipped the Developers hold.

advanced-rows.title: Advanced
advanced-rows.what: Rows that give one act apart from the levels, such as forking a thread or archiving a place. Whoever holds the level they belong with holds them too.

page-private.title: Private
page-private.what: A private page stops following its place: only its owners and the people named on it hold anything. Putting it back makes it follow the place again, and the names on it stop being named.
page-private.which: To keep a page to a few people: make it private and name them. To go back to what the place decides: choose the place’s name.

goes-environment.title: Let them into the environment
goes-environment.what: A thread runs in an environment, and its files, processes, browsers and displays are that environment’s, given on its own page. This names the people just added there to look, and with Can manage of the thread to change files and open a shell too.

goes-model.title: Include the model
goes-model.what: Talking to an agent needs the right to use the model it runs on, which is a permission on the provider’s page. This gives it to everyone who can talk to this thread, for the model and effort in use.

agents-whose.title: Whose agents
agents-whose.what: The agents of a place are every agent thread in it, those started later among them. Sharing with one thread’s agent reaches that thread alone.

agents-areas.title: What they know
agents-areas.what: Conversations are what the agents did, chats are what people said, and documents are what people wrote. Each is shared apart: not at all, to read, or to read and write.

agents-manage.title: Can manage
agents-manage.what: Agents that manage documents may also remove them, move them and bring them back. Nothing is destroyed: what they remove can be brought back until it is purged.

agents-copy.title: A copy
agents-copy.what: A copy is the thing as it is now, written as files into one agent’s workspace. It does not change afterwards, and it can be taken back.
agents-copy.which: To hand an agent a snapshot to work from: give a copy. To let it read what is written later too: keep it shared.

agents-live.title: Keep it shared
agents-live.what: The agents read it through Orch whenever they work, what is written later included, until you end it. Nothing is copied.

agents-download.title: They may download it
agents-download.what: Downloading is taking away: the agents write what they read into their workspace as files. Untick it to let them read and search it and not copy it.

line-custom.title: Custom
line-custom.what: Holds some permissions of this page but none of the three choices whole. The full form shows each row.

setting-lock.title: Lock for places below
setting-lock.what: A locked value is the same in every place below this one, and nobody there can change it. Lock what everybody inside has to follow.

thread-states.title: Thread states
thread-states.what: The icon shows what the thread is doing. A finished check stays until you see its latest turn.

reference-access.title: References and access
reference-access.what: A locked reference keeps the name that was shared. Ask for access in its card.

people-mentions.title: People and mentions
people-mentions.what: Choose whether to notify or give access after mentioning someone.

resource-facts.title: Resource facts
resource-facts.what: Read availability, measured use and limits before choosing.

references.title: References
references.what: Preview a thing or part, open it, or copy a reference an agent can follow.

live-work.title: Live progress
live-work.what: Counts and copy figures describe reported work; stopping waits for the machines.

status-items.title: Status items
status-items.what: Choose which live facts appear in the status bar, header and live line.

mount-fates.title: Mount choices
mount-fates.what: Choose what follows a move, fork or switch, and check eligible synced copies.

skills.title: Skill versions
skills.what: Publish reviewed files, then enable a version for a place's threads.

plan-mode.title: Plan
plan-mode.what: Ask for a plan before changes; the approval mode stays as shown.

plan-answer.title: Plan answer
plan-answer.what: Proceed implements the plan; Keep planning asks for a revision.

switch-history.title: History
switch-history.what: Carry, summarize or leave the conversation when switching or forking.

held-model.title: Model and environment access
held-model.what: A held input waits for someone who can drive the thread and use its model and its environment.

announcements.title: Announcements
announcements.what: Review the audience, delivery and wake choices before sending.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.what: Read notices, mark work read and choose when to be told.

loss-declare.title: Declare lost
loss-declare.what: Permanently revokes the missing machine identities and lists affected work before confirmation.

loss-recover.title: Recover environments
loss-recover.what: Choose an independent action and destination for each environment you manage.

loss-switch.title: Destination environment
loss-switch.what: Use an existing environment or make one shared environment for this batch.

loss-notify.title: Notify people
loss-notify.what: Counts only people who will receive this kind under their own notification settings.

loss-native.title: MCP offerings
loss-native.what: An imported server keeps its definition without a machine; a different definition needs an explicit choice.

loss-mounts.title: Lost mount locations
loss-mounts.what: The mount stays enabled without a location; lost locations keep their last known size.

loss-providers.title: Re-create a provider runtime
loss-providers.what: Keeps the provider settings and permissions while making a fresh runtime elsewhere.

loss-delete-host.title: Delete a host
loss-delete-host.what: Review environments, mount locations, MCP offerings and provider runtimes before removing the host.

resource-library.title: Resource library
resource-library.what: Given shows where a resource is available now. Used counts real reported work.
resource-library.which: Each view includes the ones above it. This page remembers its view, order and filters on this device.

navigation-arrangements.title: Tree and Recent
navigation-arrangements.what: Tree keeps your places together. Recent lists what you opened or what was last active.

related-items.title: Related
related-items.what: Find readable documents, chats and threads by meaning, place and references. Place and references still work when meaning is off.

document-links.title: Links
document-links.what: See what refers to this document, with the line around each mention, what it refers to, what is related and the graph around it. Only what you may read is shown.

goals.title: Goals
goals.what: Keeps the agent working until Done when holds, checked on its evidence.

keys.finder: Find anything, or run a command

tip.close: Got it, do not show this again

search.label: Search the help
search.nothingAbout: Try other words. Settings and commands are found with the finder.

articles.missing: There is no article at this address
articles.untranslated: This article is shown in English.

finder.namesPartial: More names may match. Type more letters to narrow the list.
finder.namesMinimum: Type at least two characters to find names.
finder.moreInEverythingAbout: Open the complete, paged list for these words.
finder.nothingFocused: The “{{focus}}” focus is on. Turn it off to include other things you can see.
finder.title: Find

offers.helpAbout: What it is for, its keys and the articles that belong to it

card.sharesAbout: Places, threads and documents either of you gave directly to the other, which you can both still open. Choose one to open its Access page.
card.noShares: No current direct shares to show.

bare.commands: Type what you want to do.
bare.people: Type a name, a username or an address.
bare.settings: Type what a setting does, or what a permission allows.
bare.help: Type a question, or the name of an article.
bare.conversations: Type the words to look for in conversations, chats and documents.

finder.nothingAbout: Try fewer letters, or type > for commands, @ for people, / to search what was said.

adminMode.busy: The session mode is changing. Try again in a moment.

create.type: Type a name to choose where
create.threadPlace: Choose a topic or project to start a thread.

words.switch: switch change provider agent model runtime
words.admin: admin administrator session reach permissions on off
words.appearance: theme dark light mode appearance colour color
words.bar: sidebar panel bar show hide toggle
words.signOut: sign out log out logout leave

newest.name: Newest first
newest.description: Show the most recently written matches first.

relevance.name: Best matches

docker_socket.own_kernel: the host's Docker socket cannot be reached from a virtual machine; ask for Docker inside instead

restoreBlocks.stale: The deletion changed. This old selection cannot bring it back.
restoreBlocks.unknown: The original deletion identity was not recorded.
restoreBlocks.parent_first: Bring back {{name}} first. Its restoration needs separate authority.

trace.restoreUnavailable: That restoration is no longer available. Refresh the trail to see the current job or authority.

trace.retainedApproval: Recorded request. Decisions remain read-only here.

trace.contentGuard: Looking and restoring require the thing’s current restoration authority.

trace.inspectFailure: Could not look at this deleted thing
trace.keptLead: Files still use disk space. Removing the unit did not remove these files.

trace.removalConnected: Only its registration is removed; its files stay on this machine.

trace.removalKindUnknown: The machine has not reported how this environment runs. Reconnect it to review what will be deleted.

ports.linkRequired: Use the link you were given; this address alone gives no entry.

ports.notAllowed: This audience is not allowed here.
ports.countUnknown: The complete audience count is not available.
