ports.udpNoProxy: UDP has no PROXY header. Use inside peer lookup to identify callers.
ports.affectsOpenings: These shared program options also affect: {{names}}.
ports.truncated: Some connections are outside the retained bound. Totals include Other.
ports.recentWindow: Recent ended connections: fifteen minutes, at most 128 per opening and 2048 per environment.
ports.hostAckUnknown: Saved values are shown. The host’s acknowledgement has not been reported.
ports.tokenStdin: Supply a scoped sign-in token on standard input, never in the command.
ports.webhookPath: Keep orch_token in the query when adding your service path. A POST needs no browser exchange.
ports.outsideAbout: Wider openings of environments homed here or below, including stopped environments.
ports.outsideEmpty: Nothing is open to outside here.
ports.outsidePlace: For everyone who may view {{place}}, including guests
ports.closeNeedsManage: Close requires current Ports Manage. An eligible administrator reviews the ordinary override after a refusal.

admission.decidedGrant: Allowed by {{name}}, who granted this kind to the environment
admission.grant: Opened without asking, under the grant {{name}} gave this environment
admission.template: Opened without asking: the environment’s template gives this kind
admission.policy: Opened without asking: the policy of {{place}} allows this kind

grants.title: Who agents may let in without asking
grants.about: Each kind of opening is a capability of this environment. Where it is granted here, given by the template or allowed by a place’s policy, an agent’s request opens at once; otherwise a person who manages Ports decides each request.
grants.notOffered: This environment’s template does not allow it.
grants.denied: Denied by the capability policy: nobody opens this kind here.
grants.asks: Agents ask; a person who manages Ports decides each request.
grants.granted: Granted to this environment by {{name}}: agents open it without asking.
grants.fromTemplate: Given by the template: agents open it without asking.
grants.byPolicy: Allowed by a place’s capability policy: agents open it without asking.

grantAbout.place: Agents working here may then let the viewers of a place they can see reach a port, without asking. Each such opening is listed here with this grant.
grantAbout.link: Agents working here may then make links to a port without asking, and each link goes to the agent: whoever reads its thread can use it. Each such opening is listed here with this grant.
grantAbout.host: Agents working here may then publish a port on the host to anyone who reaches it, without asking. Each such opening is listed here with this grant.

grants.revokeAbout: Agents ask again for this kind. What it opened stays open until it is closed.

cardHelp.place: Grant to this environment: this request and later ones to let a place in open without asking.
cardHelp.link: Grant to this environment: this link and later ones open without asking, and each goes to the agent that asked.
cardHelp.host: Grant to this environment: this publication on the host and later ones open without asking.

ports.staleRequest: This review is old. Read the refreshed plan before allowing it.
ports.requestPendingUntil: Pending until {{time}}; stopping the environment or ending a turn does not decide it.
ports.title: Ports
ports.about: Listeners, openings and connections of this environment.
ports.exposedReason: People beyond Ports holders may enter this port
ports.offline: Current listening is unknown while the environment is stopped or offline.
ports.unsupported: This platform cannot list scoped listeners

policy.title: Policies and limits
policy.local: The machine’s reported limits also apply. A permission in Orch does not override them.

ports.udpHttp: UDP uses the helper or a host port; a browser carries HTTP only.
ports.browserMissing: The environment’s browser is not available.
ports.internalAbout: This control listener cannot be opened outside.
ports.retained: Outside the current range · kept until Close
ports.closeAbout: This audience loses entry and its connections end. Restarting does not reopen it.
ports.placeAudience: Everyone who may view {{place}}, including guests, can use this port after signing in.
ports.placeUnchanged: This creates an opening. It does not change anyone’s permission page.
ports.forwardAbout: Run this on the device that has the connector. Supply a current scoped user token on stdin; never put it in the command.
ports.forwardPending: The connector prints the actual local address only after it binds. No local address is live yet.
ports.phoneForward: Copy this command for a device with the helper installed. It does not run on this phone by copying it.
ports.expiryHint: Required, no later than {{seconds}} seconds from now. Decided by {{scope}}.
ports.expiryInvalid: Choose a future expiry within the current maximum.
ports.linkAudience: Anyone with this link can use this port until {{time}}.
ports.linkAudienceBefore: Anyone with the link can use this port until the lapse you choose.
ports.linkWarning: The secret is shown once in this dialog. Closing it forgets the secret here.
ports.linkLost: The link exists, but its one-time secret was not received.
ports.linkLostAbout: It cannot be recovered from the opening list. Reconcile the same request, or deliberately make a new link.
ports.linkNoRecovery: Link secrets are never available from the list.
ports.hostPortHint: Optional. Leaving it empty lets the host propose a port for review.
ports.hostAudience: Anybody who reaches {{address}} reaches this. Orch does not ask them who they are.
ports.hostWarning: Orch changes no firewall. A move uses the new host’s declared address and range.
ports.candidateChanged: The reviewed candidate changed or expired. Review again before publishing.
ports.noRange: The host needs a saved address and range before publication.
ports.liveOnly: Copy address appears after the host acknowledges binding.
ports.recentConnections: Live and recent connections only; at most {{limit}} shown. Older connections are not kept here.
ports.requestTitle: An agent asks for an opening
ports.carrierHint: A browser carries HTTP only. The helper forwards raw TCP or UDP on its own device.
ports.noBrowserName: No browser address. The helper remains available.

hostForm.title: Host ports
hostForm.allAbout: All addresses means every network the machine is on.
hostForm.proposal: These values are a proposal. Publication uses them only after Save and the host’s acknowledgement.
hostForm.kept: A smaller range keeps acknowledged listeners until they close.
hostForm.closed: Changing Listens on or clearing the declaration closes affected openings.
hostForm.noFirewall: This does not configure a firewall.
hostForm.missingReview: The server has not supplied the affected allocations. Saving is unavailable until they can be reviewed.

ports.baselineAudience: You and whoever holds {{environment}}’s Ports door.
ports.stableBeforeListening: Every port keeps its address before a program starts and through its restarts. Choose a port number to see it.
ports.placeCount: {{count}} people can enter. No other environment door is given.
ports.programTitle: How the program is spoken to
ports.hostHeaderHint: Use the Host your development server expects if it refuses the outside name.
ports.tlsInside: For HTTPS inside the environment, Orch does not check the program’s certificate.
ports.linkStdin: Give the copied link on standard input. The command contains no credential.
ports.linkSharedWithAgent: This link is given to the agent and is readable in this thread.
ports.linkForMe: Only you receive this link. It is shown once here.
ports.requestDelivered: The server delivered the result to {{recipient}}.
ports.hostPortInvalid: Choose a whole port number within the declared range.
ports.hostFormInvalid: Enter a reached address, a bind choice and valid inclusive ranges.
ports.rangeHint: Inclusive ranges, for example 41000–41015. A proposal opens nothing.
ports.hostAck: Saved declaration acknowledged by the host
ports.keepOpenings: Openings stay through program and environment restarts until they expire or are closed.
ports.manageMeaning: They let more people in, make a link or publish a host port where policy allows.

craftFiles.readOnly: Files are read-only on a phone.

craftMessages.onlyYou: Only you are in this org. Create a team org to message a teammate.

fault.groupName: A group is named by 1 to {{longest}} of a to z, 0 to 9, - and _, beginning with a letter or a digit.
fault.size: Write a whole number of tokens, at least 1.
fault.largestBelowWindow: The largest context cannot be less than the model's own window ({{window}}).
fault.startAboveLargest: A thread cannot start with more than the largest ({{largest}}).
fault.startNeedsWindow: Give the model's own window first.
fault.rateInvalid: A rate is written as a number, such as 2.50.
fault.rateMissing: Give all three prices: input, cached input and output.
fault.stepIncomplete: Each step needs the size it begins at, and its input and output prices.
fault.groupsMost: A model is in at most {{most}} groups.

groups.title: Groups
groups.addHint: Name one of your own, such as frontier or small. Press Enter to add it.
groups.full: A model is in at most {{most}} groups.
groups.remove: Take it out of the group {{name}}
groups.about: A limit, an allowlist or somebody's access can name a group instead of each model.
groups.noneYet: No model is in a group yet. Put models in groups from their editor, and a limit can then name the group.

limits.title: Limits on this model
limits.lead: The caps on this provider that name this model, a family it is in, or a group it is in.
limits.none: No cap names this model, a family of it or a group of it.
limits.unavailable: The limits could not be read: {{reason}}
limits.wholeProvider_one: {{count}} cap on the whole provider covers it as well.
limits.wholeProvider_other: {{count}} caps on the whole provider cover it as well.

list.suggestionsOffer: What a suggestion offers (speeds, access programs, a larger context) is kept as offered. None of it is switched on by adding the model.

editor.title: What this model can be run with here
editor.lead: {{name}} ({{routing}}) on {{provider}}. Models differ in all of this, and the same model differs between two providers.
editor.typedIn: Typed in here: {{source}} does not list it
editor.switchedOn: Switched on, the people who may use this model here can choose it for their turns. A faster speed is counted at its own rate, and a prompt above a size may be.

efforts.title: Efforts and images
efforts.hint: The efforts it takes, separated by commas. A model that lists none takes none.

speeds.title: Speeds
speeds.lead: Service tiers beside the ordinary one, which {{source}} offers for this model. Each is off until you switch it on.
speeds.none: {{source}} offers no speed for this model. One that is not listed can still be typed in.
speeds.startHint: Standard, as shipped. A thread has this before anybody chooses; a faster speed counts at its own rate for every turn.

programs.title: Access programs
programs.lead: Programs that the vendor grants to an account, such as Codex's Daybreak. Each is off until you switch it on, and a thread also needs the place's own switch for access programs.
programs.none: No access program is offered for this model. One that is not listed can still be typed in.
programs.startHint: None, as shipped. A thread has this before anybody chooses.

context.title: Context
context.lead: How much of a conversation a thread on this model keeps. A context larger than its own window stays closed until you open it here.
context.windowHint: What its harness works with when it is told nothing. Discovery fills it in from the harness's own list; write it for a model the harness does not know.
context.largestHint: Empty until you fill it. Until then every thread on this model works with its own window, and nobody is offered more.
context.offered: Up to {{size}} · offered by {{source}} for this model
context.startWindowAbout: {{size}}. The larger context is then a choice, not the rule.
context.startWindowNone: Give its own window above first.
context.shortened: The conversation is shortened before it reaches the context, with room kept for the answer. That point is worked out; nobody sets it.
context.step: A prompt above {{size}} is counted at the rate's higher prices.
context.largestFilled: The most a thread on this model may be given. Empty it to close the larger context again.

rate.stepsHint: A request whose prompt is larger than a step pays that step's prices instead. Add as many steps as the vendor has.

everything.title: Everything
everything.sortedMatches: Best matches, your visits and activity, then {{column}}, {{direction}}
everything.empty: Nothing you can see here yet.
everything.noMatches: No names match. Try another name or clear the filters.
everything.noResults: Nothing matches these filters. Clear them to see everything again.
everything.refused: You do not have access to this view. Choose what you can see instead.
everything.sizeHint: A place totals the stored documents you can read. Resource requirements are shown where recorded.

overview.title: Overview
overview.lead: How the system stands: its parts, its queues and how they have been lately.

semantic-search.title: Semantic search
semantic-search.lead: Semantic search index of each org.

system.title: System
system.lead: The running server, the latest release and the command to run on its host.

users.title: Users
users.lead: Everybody who has an account here: make people, suspend and resume them, and give them a way back in.

orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.lead: Every root org with its owners, its size and the two limits only this screen changes.

everything.title: Everything
everything.lead: Every org's things in one tree: whose each is, what it takes and when it was last worked in.

sign-in.title: Sign-in
sign-in.lead: Who may register, how people prove who they are, and the identity providers they may use.

email.title: Channels
email.lead: The system's own ways out of the application: mail, a bot, push and webhooks.

hosts.title: Hosts
hosts.lead: Every host on the system, how much of it the environments on it declare they need, and what happens when it is full.

runtimes.title: Runtimes
runtimes.lead: Both pools on every host: environments and the runtimes of providers.

templates.title: System templates
templates.lead: The system's templates for environments and for providers' runtimes.

mcp.title: MCP presets
mcp.lead: The system's MCP servers, ready to switch on for environments.

defaults.title: Access defaults
defaults.lead: What every org starts from, and how many orgs follow each row.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.lead: What an agent can ask for, how risky it is, and who decides.

harnesses.title: Agent programs
harnesses.lead: The adapters this system has, the builds of each, and what each supports.

rates.title: Rates
rates.lead: The catalogue of estimates and the system's own rates.

agents.title: Agents
agents.lead: Agent profiles that belong to the system itself.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.lead: External implementations loaded on any part of the system.

storage.title: Storage
storage.lead: What the blob store holds, how much room is left, and which environments take the most.

pki.title: PKI
pki.lead: The authority every machine trusts, and which certificates are about to end.

audit.title: Audit
audit.lead: Everything done on the system, newest first, and a file of it for a span of days.

refusal.title: Management is for system administrators
refusal.lead: Your account is not one. Ask one of this system's administrators to make the change you need, or to make you one.

overview.partsLead: Each part reports every fifteen seconds. One that has not reported for three beats is counted as not answering.
overview.overTimeLead: What the system stored about itself: a value a minute for the last month, and a value an hour for good.

charts.waiting: Waiting for a cap or a lock

overview.nothingStored: Nothing is stored for this span yet.
overview.chartKeys: Use the left and right arrow keys to read the values at each moment.

banner.title: Notice for everybody
banner.lead: Shown across the top of every page until it ends or is taken down.
banner.textHint: One or two sentences that tell people what is happening and what to do.
banner.takeDownBody: Nobody will see it any more. Its text is not kept.

users.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, username or address
users.adminSentence: A system admin is an Admin of every org here.

create.title: Make a new user
create.lead: They receive a link to set their password.
create.usernameHint: 3 to 32 characters: lower-case letters, digits, hyphen and underscore.
create.usernameRule: Use 3 to 32 lower-case letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, beginning with a letter or a digit.
create.name: Name
create.emailHint: Where mail to them goes. They confirm it themselves.
create.ownOrgHint: These start from the system policy. Change them to let this personal org accept members or contain organizations.
create.noOwnOrg: Personal organizations are disabled for new accounts. This account can still join organizations and receive shared documents.

made.title: {{name}} is made
made.lead: Give them this link. They set their own password at it.
made.note: The link is shown now and not again. If it is lost, make a new one from the user's menu.

link.title: Reset link for {{name}}
link.lead: Makes the address at which they set a new password.
link.clear: Also switch their second step off (they lost their phone or their mailbox)
link.clearHint: Using the link then clears an authenticator and a code by mail alike.
link.noSecondStep: They have no second step set up.
link.clearDone: Using this link also switches their second step off.

suspend.title: Suspend {{name}}?
suspend.body: They cannot sign in anywhere on this system. What they own stays theirs.

resume.title: Resume {{name}}?
resume.body: They can sign in again, to everything they own.

grant.title: Make {{name}} a system admin?
grant.body: A system admin is an Admin of every org here.

revoke.title: Take away the system admin role of {{name}}?
revoke.body: They stay in every org they belong to, and stop being an Admin of all the others. The last system admin cannot be taken away.

users.acknowledge: This person is a system admin. I understand what changing them means for the system.
users.acknowledgeGrant: I understand that a system admin can read and change everything on this system.

orgInvitation.giveAbout: They may make one team org; making it uses the invitation.
orgInvitation.takeBackAbout: They have not used it yet.
orgInvitation.takenBack: {{name}} may no longer make a team org.

locked.password: Password locked for new browsers until {{time}}
locked.email_code: Code by mail locked for new browsers until {{time}}
locked.totp: Authenticator code locked for new browsers until {{time}}
locked.recovery_code: Recovery code locked for new browsers until {{time}}
locked.advice: They can sign in where they signed in before, or with a reset link.

registration.title: Who may register
registration.lead: Whoever joins gets an account here. This decides who may make one.
registration.label: Who may register

open.about: Anybody can make an account at the registration page, with an invitation or without one.

invite.about: An invitation into any org here, a department included, or one of the system's. Each root org decides which forms it gives out.

closed.about: Nobody can register. Every person is made on the Users screen and given a link to set a password.

orgs.title: Who may make an org
orgs.lead: A team org is where people work together. This decides who may make one.
orgs.label: Who may make an org

admins.about: Everybody else joins the orgs they are invited into.

anyone.about: Anybody with an account here can make a team org.

invited.about: System admins make team orgs, and so does somebody a system admin invited to make one.

orgs.whereInvitations: A system admin gives such an invitation from Users; it is used once.
orgs.ownOrg: Personal organization creation is controlled separately from team organization creation.

proofs.title: How people prove who they are
proofs.lead: Settings of the whole system. An org may hold itself to more than they say, and never to less.

verify.label: Ask new people to confirm their address
verify.hint: Somebody who registers is mailed a link and cannot sign in until they have used it.
verify.noMail: This system has no mail server, so no address can be confirmed by mail.

password.label: Sign in with a password
password.hint: When this is off, only system admins sign in with a password or a code by mail. Everybody else signs in through an identity provider.
password.nobody: No identity provider is switched on, so nobody but a system admin could sign in. Switch one on first.

code.title: A code by mail
code.lead: What a code sent to a person's confirmed address may be for.
code.signIn: A way to sign in without the password
code.secondStep: A second step after the password, for whoever switches it on
code.safety: A mailed code is as safe as the mailbox it goes to. For somebody who is in several orgs it counts only where each of them allows it.
code.lockHint: A root org can then no longer allow more than this.

signIn.noMail: This system has no mail server.
signIn.tries: Eight wrong tries at one name in three hours lock that proof for that name, wherever the tries come from. Browsers a person signed in from are counted by themselves.

providers.title: Identity providers
providers.lead: Other services people may sign in through, such as a company's single sign-on.

idp.name: Name
idp.callbackNote: Give each provider its callback address, which is shown under its name, as the address it sends people back to.
idp.noneHint: Add one to let people sign in through another service.
idp.testLead: Reads the provider's description of itself and the keys it signs with. Nobody is signed in.
idp.notFound: The provider did not answer as it should
idp.notFoundUnsaid: The test failed without saying why.
idp.formLead: What this system needs from the provider, and what a person who comes through it gets.
idp.keyHint: Part of its addresses: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.
idp.keyRule: Use 2 to 32 lower-case letters, digits or hyphens, beginning with a letter.
idp.issuerHint: The https address of the provider, without a query or a fragment; http only for a provider on this machine.
idp.issuerRule: Give an https address without a query or a fragment (http only for this machine).
idp.clientRule: Give the client id the provider made for this system.
idp.secretHint: Written here once; it is never shown again.
idp.secretKept: One is set. Leave this empty to keep it, or write a new one.
idp.scopesHint: Separated by spaces. The provider needs to give a name and an address.
idp.claims: Where it puts what we need
idp.claimsHint: The names of the claims that hold each thing. Leave them as they are unless the provider names them otherwise.
idp.domainsHint: Separated by spaces. Empty means any domain.
idp.autoRegister: Make an account on a first sign-in
idp.autoRegisterHint: Otherwise only people who have an account already can come through it.
idp.defaultOrgHint: Where a new account from this provider joins during ordinary registration. An explicit invitation follows its own target.
idp.enabledHint: Off, it is not offered at the sign-in page.
idp.stale: Somebody changed this provider while the form was open. Close it and open it again.
idp.removeBody: People can no longer sign in through it. Their accounts are kept. A provider cannot be deleted while it is someone's only sign-in method.

orgs.searchPlaceholder: Search by name or short name

closed.label: Takes members
closed.stays_one: No further members. Its {{number}} person stays.
closed.stays_other: No further members. Its {{number}} people stay.

flat.label: Holds orgs inside it
flat.stays_one: No further orgs inside it. The {{number}} org there stays.
flat.stays_other: No further orgs inside it. The {{number}} orgs there stay.

orgs.restored: {{name}} is back, archived, with everything under it
orgs.deletedLead: A deleted org can be brought back until it is purged.

owner.title: Name an owner of {{org}}
owner.lead: Its owners are gone. The person you name becomes its first owner.
owner.hint: Somebody who is a member of this org.

hosts.policyLead: Settings of the whole system. A host that says nothing of its own follows them.
hosts.fullFrom: A host counts as full from
hosts.fullFromHint: Of the memory it reports, once the units on it declare they need that much. Nothing is reserved for them, so a host that grows on demand can take more than it shows.
hosts.whenFull: Where a host says nothing of its own, being full
hosts.whenFullHint: A host's own page can say otherwise for that host.
hosts.whenFullWarn: Warn, and let the host answer
hosts.listLead: The system's own, and those members added for their orgs.

does.warn: Warns, and lets the host answer

hosts.noneHint: Add one from a machine in Resources.
hosts.note: Memory is what the units on a host declare they need, out of what the host reports. Nothing of it is reserved.

runtimes.updateNote_one: {{number}} unit is behind. Open it by its name to update it.
runtimes.updateNote_other: {{number}} units are behind. Open one by its name to update it.

allow.label: Give it
allow.about: An agent that asks is given it at once.

ask.label: Ask the approver
ask.about: The request waits until its approver answers.

deny.label: Refuse it
deny.about: The request is refused at once.

scopes.environment: The holders of Ports Manage on this environment
scopes.org: The admins of the environment's home org

capabilities.shipsReason: It ships with Orch, and would come back at the next start.
capabilities.formLead: What it is called, how risky it is, who decides, and what each driver does to give it.
capabilities.keyHint: What agents ask for by. It cannot be changed afterwards.
capabilities.keyRule: Use 2 to 32 lower-case letters, digits or underscores, beginning with a letter.
capabilities.label: Name
capabilities.patchHint: An object whose members are driver names, each holding what that driver merges into the unit it makes.
capabilities.patchRule: This is not a JSON object.
capabilities.stale: Somebody changed this definition while the form was open. Close it and open it again.
capabilities.removeBody: Agents can no longer request it. A capability cannot be deleted while an environment still holds it.

harnesses.sourceHelp: The checksum source names who supplied the expected program bytes. A compatibility check keeps that source.
